response_guidance: For unapproved deletions of Tier-0/DC objects, treat as a potential destructive-attack indicator and engage incident response immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Computer Account Password Reset Outside Normal 30-Day Machine Cycle
description: Windows machines automatically rotate their computer-account password roughly every 30 days. A manual, out-of-cycle reset of a computer account's password (via Reset-ComputerMachinePassword, netdom, or LDAP attribute write) can indicate an attacker regaining control of a computer account whose credential material they possess (e.g. after extracting it for Silver Ticket forgery), or preparing the account for RBCD abuse where they need a known password.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 4742 (computer account changed) correlated with password-reset indicator.

detection_logic: Event ID 4742 where the change reflects a password reset performed by an interactive/non-machine principal rather than the computer itself.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4742
| where Subject_Account_Name!=Target_Account_Name+"$"
| lookup computer_account_src_baseline.csv Subject_Account_Name OUTPUT is_baseline
| where isnull(is_baseline)
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Target_Account_Name
tuning_guidance: 4742 fires for many benign attribute changes; scope to environments where a password-change flag can be isolated, or supplement with Sysmon/PowerShell script-block logging for Reset-ComputerMachinePassword/netdom resetpwd.
investigation_steps: Identify who/what reset the password and why.
Check whether the computer account is Tier-0 or has delegation configured.
Review recent authentication using the computer account's new credentials.
response_guidance: Validate against a change ticket; if unexplained, treat the computer account as potentially compromised and review its delegation/SPN configuration.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: 4742 covers many computer-object attribute changes, not password resets specifically; this detection is best-effort without a dedicated password-change field.

title: Computer Account Authenticating from Multiple Concurrent IP Addresses
description: A computer account's Kerberos/NTLM authentication should originate from the physical or virtual host that owns it. A single computer account authenticating concurrently from multiple distinct source IPs can indicate an attacker has extracted the computer account's credential material (e.g. from LSASS or the registry SECRETS hive) and is replaying it from an attacker-controlled host.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 4624 for machine-account (Sam_Account_Name ending in $) logons.

detection_logic: Event ID 4624 where Account_Name ends in '$'; group by Account_Name over a 15-minute window; alert when distinct_count(Source_Network_Address) > 1 and addresses are not both known NAT/load-balanced ranges.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4624 Account_Name="*$"
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats dc(Source_Network_Address) as src_count values(Source_Network_Address) as sources by _time, Account_Name
| where src_count > 1
tuning_guidance: Exclude known clustered/load-balanced service hosts and DHCP-churn ranges via a computer_account_src_baseline.csv lookup.
investigation_steps: Identify both source hosts and confirm which one legitimately owns the computer account.
Check for signs of credential-dumping tooling on the legitimate host.
Review what the illegitimate source authenticated to.
response_guidance: Reset the computer account password immediately (this invalidates cached tickets/hashes) and isolate the illegitimate source.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Domain-Controller Computer Account Used for Interactive-Style Authentication
description: A domain controller's own computer account (DC01$ etc.) authenticating outward as a client — e.g. NTLM logon to a file share, or an interactive logon type 2/10 using the DC computer account — is a strong indicator of NTLM relay/coercion abuse (PetitPotam, PrinterBug, DFSCoerce) where the DC has been coerced into authenticating to an attacker-controlled listener, or of an attacker directly using extracted DC computer-account credentials.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: Target-host security event log, Event ID 4624/4776 for the DC machine account as source identity.

detection_logic: Event ID 4624/4776 on a non-DC host where Account_Name matches a known domain_controllers.csv computer account.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" (EventCode=4624 OR EventCode=4776)
| lookup domain_controllers.csv computer_name AS Account_Name OUTPUT is_dc
| where is_dc=1
| lookup domain_controllers.csv computer_name AS dvc OUTPUT is_dc_dest
| where isnull(is_dc_dest)
| table _time, dvc, Account_Name, Logon_Type, Source_Network_Address
tuning_guidance: This is a critical control detection with an intentionally narrow, high-signal scope: alert on all matches after confirming the destination is not itself a DC (DC-to-DC replication traffic is expected and must be excluded).
investigation_steps: Identify the destination host and service the DC authenticated to.
Check for coercion tooling indicators (PetitPotam/PrinterBug/DFSCoerce) on the destination or an intermediate relay host.
Review whether NTLM relay to LDAP/LDAPS/ADCS occurred immediately after.
response_guidance: Treat as a likely active NTLM-relay attack against the DC; isolate the destination host, patch/mitigate the coercion vector (disable EFS-RPC/print spooler on DCs), and enforce LDAP signing/channel binding domain-wide.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Computer Object Moved to a Different Organizational Unit
description: Detects a computer object being moved between OUs. Moving a computer into an OU with weaker GPO security settings, less restrictive delegation, or out of an OU covered by a monitoring GPO can be used to strip security controls or evade policy enforcement ahead of further attack activity.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 4741/4742 with DN change, or directory-service-changes 5136 on distinguishedName.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name=distinguishedName and objectClass=computer.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="distinguishedName"
| search Object_Class=computer
| lookup tier0_ous.csv target_ou OUTPUT is_tier0_ou
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, Attribute_Value, is_tier0_ou
tuning_guidance: Requires Directory Service Changes auditing enabled on the DC (Advanced Audit Policy > DS Access). Escalate any move into or out of a Tier-0 OU.
investigation_steps: Confirm the move against a change ticket.
Compare GPOs applied before and after the move.
Check for a subsequent suspicious action from the moved computer.
response_guidance: Move the object back if unauthorized and review the actor's OU-move delegation rights.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: High Volume of Computer Account Creations Domain-Wide
description: Detects an abnormal domain-wide spike in computer-account creation events across multiple actors/sources — a pattern consistent with automated RBCD staging, a compromised provisioning pipeline, or a worm-like AD-abuse tool sweeping MachineAccountQuota across many user contexts.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 4741 aggregated domain-wide.

detection_logic: Event ID 4741 count domain-wide over 1 hour compared against a 14-day rolling baseline; alert when current count exceeds baseline mean + 3 standard deviations.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4741
| bucket _time span=1h
| stats count as created_count by _time
| eventstats avg(created_count) as avg_count, stdev(created_count) as std_count
| where created_count > (avg_count + 3*std_count) AND created_count > 5
tuning_guidance: Requires at least 14 days of history to build a meaningful baseline; suppress during known bulk-provisioning maintenance windows.
investigation_steps: Break down the spike by Subject_Account_Name to identify whether it is one actor or many.
Cross-reference with AD-COMP-002 for any single-actor bursts within the spike.
response_guidance: If unexplained, treat as a fleet-wide RBCD-staging event and audit all newly created computer objects for delegation attributes.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Computer Account SPN Modified to Add High-Value Service Class
description: Detects a servicePrincipalName attribute added to a computer account for a high-value service class (e.g. MSSQLSvc, HTTP, CIFS on a Tier-0 host) by an actor other than the expected service-installation account. Adding an SPN to an attacker-controlled or attacker-influenced computer account is a step toward Kerberoasting or Silver Ticket abuse targeting that service.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on servicePrincipalName for objectClass=computer.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name=servicePrincipalName, Object_Class=computer, and Attribute_Value matches a high-value SPN pattern.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="servicePrincipalName" Object_Class=computer
| lookup high_value_spns.csv spn_prefix AS Attribute_Value OUTPUT is_high_value
| where is_high_value=1
| lookup service_accounts.csv Subject_Account_Name OUTPUT is_expected_installer
| where isnull(is_expected_installer)
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, Attribute_Value
tuning_guidance: Requires DS Access auditing. Maintain high_value_spns.csv with service-class prefixes considered sensitive (MSSQLSvc, HTTP on Tier-0, etc.).
investigation_steps: Confirm a legitimate service-installation change ticket exists.
Check whether the computer account is later Kerberoasted (correlate with AD-KRB-009/010/011).
Review the actor's rights to modify this computer object.
response_guidance: Remove unauthorized SPNs and review the actor's delegated write access to the object.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Stale Computer Account Suddenly Active After Long Dormancy
description: Detects authentication from a computer account whose password has not changed and which has shown no logon activity for an extended period (e.g. 180+ days), suddenly authenticating again. Dormant computer accounts are attractive targets because their credential compromise is less likely to be noticed and they are prime candidates for reactivation as an RBCD impersonation identity or a persistence foothold.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 4768/4624 for the computer account, compared to ad_last_login.csv.

detection_logic: Event ID 4768 (TGT request) or 4624 for Account_Name ending in '$' where lookup against ad_last_login.csv shows no prior activity within 180 days.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" (EventCode=4768 OR EventCode=4624) Account_Name="*$"
| lookup ad_last_login.csv account AS Account_Name OUTPUT last_seen
| eval days_dormant=round((now()-strptime(last_seen,"%Y-%m-%d"))/86400)
| where days_dormant >= 180
| table _time, dvc, Account_Name, days_dormant
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained ad_last_login.csv baseline generated from a periodic LastLogonTimestamp export.
investigation_steps: Confirm whether the physical/virtual host still exists and was legitimately re-provisioned.
Check for delegation attributes newly configured on the account.
Review what the reactivated account authenticated to.
response_guidance: If unexplained, disable the account and reset its password pending investigation; consider a periodic stale-computer-account cleanup process.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Computer Account Name Does Not Match Naming Convention
description: Detects newly created computer accounts whose sAMAccountName does not conform to the organization's asset-naming standard. Attacker-created computer accounts (e.g. via impacket addcomputer.py) often use default or random names that stand out from a consistent corporate naming scheme, or deliberately mimic legitimate hostnames to blend in — both patterns are worth reviewing.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 4741.

detection_logic: Event ID 4741 where Sam_Account_Name does not match the configured regex naming pattern.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4741
| eval matches_convention=if(match(Sam_Account_Name, "^(DC|SRV|WKS|LT)-[A-Z0-9]+\$$"), 1, 0)
| where matches_convention=0
| table _time, dvc, Sam_Account_Name, Subject_Account_Name
tuning_guidance: The regex must be tailored per environment; treat this as a low-confidence hygiene check rather than a standalone high-fidelity alert. Combine with AD-COMP-001 for higher confidence.
investigation_steps: Confirm the naming pattern used by this organization.
Review who created the account and why.
response_guidance: Rename or investigate non-conforming accounts per local process; not independently actionable.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Computer Account Created and Deleted Within a Short Window (Hit-and-Run Pattern)
description: Detects a computer account that is created and then deleted within a short window (e.g. under 4 hours) — a pattern consistent with an attacker staging a temporary computer account for an RBCD attack and then removing it to reduce forensic footprint, rather than the typical multi-day/week lifecycle of a legitimate asset.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 4741 (create) and 4743 (delete), correlated by Sam_Account_Name.

detection_logic: Event ID 4741 followed by Event ID 4743 for the same Sam_Account_Name within 4 hours.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" (EventCode=4741 OR EventCode=4743)
| transaction Sam_Account_Name startswith=eval(EventCode=4741) endswith=eval(EventCode=4743) maxspan=4h
| where eventcount=2
| table _time, dvc, Sam_Account_Name, Subject_Account_Name, duration
tuning_guidance: Exclude known automated test/imaging pipelines that legitimately create and tear down computer objects rapidly.
investigation_steps: Review all authentication and delegation-attribute activity that occurred on the account during its short lifetime.
Identify the creating/deleting actor and confirm whether they are the same identity.
response_guidance: Treat as a probable RBCD hit-and-run; audit the creating actor's other recent activity for a broader attack chain.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Domain Controller Computer Account Object Modified
description: Detects any modification to a computer object known to be a domain controller (userAccountControl, servicePrincipalName, dNSHostName, or delegation attributes). DC computer objects should change rarely, only through well-known administrative or promotion/demotion processes; unexpected modification can be a precursor to DCShadow-style attacks or delegation abuse targeting Tier-0.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 4742 where Target_Account_Name is a known DC.

detection_logic: Event ID 4742 where Target_Account_Name is present in domain_controllers.csv.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4742
| lookup domain_controllers.csv computer_name AS Target_Account_Name OUTPUT is_dc
| where is_dc=1
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Target_Account_Name
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches; DC computer-object changes are rare enough that this should be a near-zero-noise critical control once domain_controllers.csv is accurate.
investigation_steps: Identify exactly which attribute changed.
Confirm against a documented DC-maintenance/promotion-demotion change window.
Check the actor's rights and whether they are a known AD administrator.
response_guidance: Treat any unapproved change as a potential Tier-0 compromise indicator; engage incident response immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota Attribute Modified
description: Detects modification of the domain-level ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota attribute. An attacker with sufficient rights may raise this value to make additional computer-account creation available to more principals, or an administrator may legitimately lower it to 0 as a hardening measure — either way this is a domain-wide security-posture change worth reviewing.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name=ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota"
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Attribute_Value
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches; this attribute should change only as part of a deliberate, documented hardening or provisioning-policy decision.
investigation_steps: Confirm the change against a documented policy decision.
If the value was raised, review why and by whom.
response_guidance: If unauthorized and raised, revert to 0 (recommended hardening baseline) and audit the actor's other AD write activity.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Computer Account Granted msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity (RBCD Configured)
description: Detects the msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity attribute being set on a computer object — the attribute that configures Resource-Based Constrained Delegation (RBCD). Legitimate RBCD configuration is rare and deliberate (e.g. certain clustering/gMSA scenarios); attacker-configured RBCD lets a compromised/attacker-controlled computer account impersonate any user to the target resource, including Domain Admins, via S4U2Self/S4U2Proxy.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name=msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity and the object is not present in an approved-RBCD lookup.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity"
| lookup approved_rbcd_configurations.csv object_dn AS Object_DN OUTPUT is_approved
| where isnull(is_approved)
| lookup tier0_computers.csv computer_name AS Object_DN OUTPUT is_tier0
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, is_tier0
tuning_guidance: This is one of the highest-value RBCD detections in the library — alert on all matches and treat is_tier0=1 as Critical regardless of confidence, per the master detection requirements. Maintain approved_rbcd_configurations.csv for the rare legitimate cases.
investigation_steps: Identify the trustee SID(s) written into the attribute and resolve them to accounts.
Correlate with AD-COMP-001/002 to check whether the trustee is a recently self-created computer account (the classic RBCD chain).
Check for S4U2Proxy ticket requests immediately following.
response_guidance: Remove the unauthorized delegation attribute immediately; treat as an active privilege-escalation attempt and investigate the configuring actor's full session.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: GenericAll Right Granted on a Privileged Object
description: Detects an ACE granting GenericAll (full control) to a security principal on a privileged object — a user, group, computer, GPO, or OU flagged Tier-0. GenericAll allows the trustee to fully control the object, including resetting passwords, adding group memberships, and modifying any attribute. Attackers use DACL abuse (via tools like BloodHound-identified paths) to grant themselves or a controlled principal this right as a durable, hard-to-notice persistence mechanism, since the target object's own security-relevant attributes remain unchanged.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on nTSecurityDescriptor for Tier-0 objects.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name=nTSecurityDescriptor, the object is in tier0_objects.csv, and the new ACE grants GenericAll (0x10000000 / ObjectType wildcard) to a principal not in expected_adminsdholder_trustees.csv.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="nTSecurityDescriptor"
| lookup tier0_objects.csv object_dn AS Object_DN OUTPUT is_tier0
| where is_tier0=1
| rex field=Attribute_Value "AceType=(?<ace_type>\S+).*Mask=(?<ace_mask>0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+).*Trustee=(?<trustee>\S+)"
| where ace_mask="0x10000000" OR ace_mask="0xf01ff"
| lookup expected_adminsdholder_trustees.csv trustee OUTPUT is_expected
| where isnull(is_expected)
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, trustee, ace_mask
tuning_guidance: Requires DS Access auditing and an accurate tier0_objects.csv (Domain Admins/Enterprise Admins members, DCs, AdminSDHolder, Tier-0 GPOs/OUs). Alert on all matches for confirmed Tier-0 objects.
investigation_steps: Resolve the trustee SID to a principal.
Determine who granted the ACE and their own privilege level.
Use BloodHound or a similar tool to assess whether this creates a new attack path to Domain Admins.
response_guidance: Remove the unauthorized ACE immediately and audit the granting actor's own access rights and recent activity for the initial compromise vector.
author: Threat Detection Library
performance_guidance: ACE parsing from the raw SDDL/Attribute_Value string is expensive at scale; restrict this search to objects already flagged Tier-0 via lookup rather than scanning all 5136 events.

title: WriteDACL Right Granted on a Privileged Object
description: Detects an ACE granting WriteDACL to a security principal on a Tier-0 object. WriteDACL lets the trustee modify the object's own DACL — including granting itself GenericAll afterward — making it an equally dangerous, often less-scrutinized precursor to full-control persistence.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on nTSecurityDescriptor, ACE mask WRITE_DAC (0x40000).

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where the new ACE grants WRITE_DAC on a Tier-0 object to an unexpected trustee.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="nTSecurityDescriptor"
| lookup tier0_objects.csv object_dn AS Object_DN OUTPUT is_tier0
| where is_tier0=1
| rex field=Attribute_Value "Mask=(?<ace_mask>0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+).*Trustee=(?<trustee>\S+)"
| where ace_mask="0x40000"
| lookup expected_adminsdholder_trustees.csv trustee OUTPUT is_expected
| where isnull(is_expected)
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, trustee
tuning_guidance: Same lookup dependencies as AD-ACL-001; alert on all matches for Tier-0 objects.
investigation_steps: Resolve trustee and granting actor.
Check whether the trustee subsequently modified the DACL further (chained ACL escalation).
response_guidance: Remove the unauthorized ACE and audit the granting actor.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: WriteOwner Right Granted or Object Owner Changed on a Privileged Object
description: Detects the owner attribute of a Tier-0 object being changed, or an ACE granting WriteOwner. The object owner implicitly has WriteDACL rights regardless of the DACL contents, making an owner change one of the most potent and easily overlooked persistence primitives — an attacker who becomes owner of a privileged group can grant itself further rights even after the original ACE abuse is remediated.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on nTSecurityDescriptor Owner field.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where the security descriptor's Owner SID changes on a Tier-0 object, or a WRITE_OWNER (0x80000) ACE is added.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="nTSecurityDescriptor"
| lookup tier0_objects.csv object_dn AS Object_DN OUTPUT is_tier0
| where is_tier0=1
| rex field=Attribute_Value "Owner=(?<new_owner>\S+)"
| lookup expected_object_owners.csv object_dn AS Object_DN OUTPUT expected_owner
| where isnotnull(new_owner) AND new_owner!=expected_owner
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, new_owner, expected_owner
tuning_guidance: Maintain expected_object_owners.csv (normally Domain Admins/Enterprise Admins) for all Tier-0 objects. Alert on all matches.
investigation_steps: Determine how the actor obtained WriteOwner in the first place (this is usually a secondary abuse step after another ACL grant).
Revert ownership and audit the full ACL for further tampering.
response_guidance: Revert the object owner to the expected principal immediately; this is a near-certain indicator of an active ACL-abuse persistence chain.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: GenericWrite Right Granted on a Privileged Object
description: Detects an ACE granting GenericWrite to a security principal on a Tier-0 object. GenericWrite allows writing most attributes, including scriptPath (logon-script persistence) on a user object or member on a group — enough for an attacker to add themselves to a privileged group without needing full control.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on nTSecurityDescriptor, ACE mask GENERIC_WRITE (0x40000000).

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where the new ACE grants GENERIC_WRITE on a Tier-0 object to an unexpected trustee.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="nTSecurityDescriptor"
| lookup tier0_objects.csv object_dn AS Object_DN OUTPUT is_tier0
| where is_tier0=1
| rex field=Attribute_Value "Mask=(?<ace_mask>0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+).*Trustee=(?<trustee>\S+)"
| where ace_mask="0x40000000"
| lookup expected_adminsdholder_trustees.csv trustee OUTPUT is_expected
| where isnull(is_expected)
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, trustee
tuning_guidance: Same lookup pattern as AD-ACL-001/002.
investigation_steps: Resolve trustee and check for a subsequent group-membership or scriptPath write using the new right.
Correlate with AD-GRP entries for privileged group additions immediately following.
response_guidance: Remove the ACE and audit the granting actor.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: ResetPassword Extended Right Granted on a Privileged User Object
description: Detects the User-Force-Change-Password extended right (ResetPassword) being granted on a Tier-0 user object. This right lets the trustee reset the target user's password without knowing the current one — a direct, minimal-footprint path to account takeover once granted, frequently used in ACL-abuse attack chains against Domain Admin members or service accounts with elevated rights.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on nTSecurityDescriptor, ObjectType GUID for User-Force-Change-Password (00299570-246d-11d0-a768-00aa006e0529).

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where the new ACE's ObjectType matches the User-Force-Change-Password control-access-right GUID on a Tier-0 or privileged-service-account user object.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="nTSecurityDescriptor"
| lookup tier0_privileged_accounts.csv object_dn AS Object_DN OUTPUT is_privileged
| where is_privileged=1
| search Attribute_Value="*00299570-246d-11d0-a768-00aa006e0529*"
| rex field=Attribute_Value "Trustee=(?<trustee>\S+)"
| lookup expected_adminsdholder_trustees.csv trustee OUTPUT is_expected
| where isnull(is_expected)
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, trustee
tuning_guidance: Maintain tier0_privileged_accounts.csv with full DN coverage of Domain Admin/Enterprise Admin/high-value service accounts. Alert on all matches.
investigation_steps: Resolve trustee and check whether a password reset was actually executed afterward (correlate AD-USER-013).
Determine the initial access the granting actor used.
response_guidance: Remove the ACE immediately and force a password reset on the target privileged account via a trusted process.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: ResetPassword Right Granted Followed by Immediate Password Reset (Chain)
description: The flagship ACL-to-credential-takeover chain: an actor is granted ResetPassword rights on a privileged user object, and shortly afterward actually resets that user's password. This sequence has very few legitimate explanations outside a documented delegated helpdesk workflow and represents near-certain account takeover of the target privileged identity.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 (ACE grant) and 4724 (password reset) correlated by actor and target.

detection_logic: AD-ACL-005 match followed within 24 hours by an Event ID 4724 (password reset) from the same trustee against the same target object.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" (EventCode=5136 OR EventCode=4724)
| eval etype=if(EventCode=5136, "ace_grant", "pw_reset")
| transaction Target_Account_Name maxspan=24h startswith=eval(etype="ace_grant") endswith=eval(etype="pw_reset")
| where eventcount=2
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Target_Account_Name, duration
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches; suppress only for a documented, lookup-verified delegated-helpdesk workflow.
investigation_steps: Immediately review whether the target account has since authenticated.
Assume credential compromise and initiate incident response.
response_guidance: Treat as an active, likely successful account-takeover chain; force another password reset via a trusted out-of-band process, revoke sessions/tickets, and remove the ACL grant.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: AllExtendedRights Granted on a Privileged Object
description: Detects an ACE granting All-Extended-Rights (the wildcard control-access right, which includes ResetPassword, DS-Replication-Get-Changes, and every other extended right in one grant) to a security principal on a Tier-0 object. This is functionally equivalent to granting the trustee every sensitive extended capability at once, including DCSync rights if granted at the domain root.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on nTSecurityDescriptor, ObjectType GUID 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 with ADS_RIGHT_DS_CONTROL_ACCESS mask.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where the new ACE grants ADS_RIGHT_DS_CONTROL_ACCESS (0x100) with a null/wildcard ObjectType on a Tier-0 object.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="nTSecurityDescriptor"
| lookup tier0_objects.csv object_dn AS Object_DN OUTPUT is_tier0
| where is_tier0=1
| rex field=Attribute_Value "Mask=(?<ace_mask>0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+).*ObjectType=(?<obj_type>[0-9a-fA-F-]+).*Trustee=(?<trustee>\S+)"
| where ace_mask="0x100" AND (obj_type="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000" OR obj_type="")
| lookup expected_adminsdholder_trustees.csv trustee OUTPUT is_expected
| where isnull(is_expected)
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, trustee
tuning_guidance: If Object_DN corresponds to the domain root or a naming-context object, treat as equivalent-priority to a DCSync-rights grant (see AD-REPL namespace) — alert on all matches.
investigation_steps: Determine the object scope (single account vs. domain root) — domain-root grants are catastrophic.
Resolve trustee and check for subsequent DS-Replication-Get-Changes use.
response_guidance: Remove the ACE immediately; if granted at the domain root, treat as a DCSync-rights compromise and follow the same response procedure as AD-REPL DCSync detections.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: ACE Added to a Non-Privileged Object by a Non-Administrative Actor
description: A broader, lower-confidence complement to AD-ACL-001 through 007: detects any actor who is not a member of a recognized AD-administration group making a DACL modification on any object, including non-Tier-0 objects. Useful for catching ACL-abuse attack-path staging against mid-tier objects (e.g. OU delegation abuse, help-desk-scoped accounts) that BloodHound-style analysis shows can be chained toward Tier-0.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on nTSecurityDescriptor.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 on nTSecurityDescriptor where Subject_Account_Name is not present in authorized_identity_admins.csv.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="nTSecurityDescriptor"
| lookup authorized_identity_admins.csv Subject_Account_Name OUTPUT is_admin
| where isnull(is_admin)
| stats count by _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN
tuning_guidance: Expect meaningfully higher volume/noise than the Tier-0-scoped ACL detections; route to a lower-priority queue and use primarily for periodic attack-path review rather than real-time alerting.
investigation_steps: Batch-review weekly; feed changed objects into a BloodHound path-to-Tier-0 analysis.
Escalate any object found to have a new path to a privileged group.
response_guidance: Not independently actionable per-event; use to drive periodic attack-path graph review and delegation cleanup.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Inheritance Disabled on a Privileged Object's ACL
description: Detects the security-descriptor control flags on a Tier-0 object changing to disable ACL inheritance (SE_DACL_PROTECTED). Disabling inheritance freezes the object's explicit ACEs so they are no longer overwritten by parent-container policy or SDProp, letting an attacker's previously added ACE persist even after broader remediation efforts that rely on inheritance to clean up permissions.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on nTSecurityDescriptor control flags.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where the security-descriptor control flags for a Tier-0 object transition to SE_DACL_PROTECTED (P flag in SDDL).
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="nTSecurityDescriptor"
| lookup tier0_objects.csv object_dn AS Object_DN OUTPUT is_tier0
| where is_tier0=1
| rex field=Attribute_Value "^D:(?<dacl_flags>P?A?R?)"
| where like(dacl_flags, "P%")
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN
tuning_guidance: AdminSDHolder-protected objects are expected to already have inheritance disabled (that is what SDProp does) — exclude objects already tagged as SDProp-protected in sdprop_protected_objects.csv and focus on non-protected Tier-0 objects transitioning unexpectedly.
investigation_steps: Determine why inheritance was disabled and by whom.
Review the object's full explicit ACL for unexpected ACEs added at the same time.
response_guidance: Re-enable inheritance if unauthorized and review the full ACL for other tampering.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All Right Granted Outside Domain Controllers Group
description: Detects the DS-Replication-Get-Changes and DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All extended rights being granted at the domain naming-context level to a principal that is not a domain controller, Enterprise/Domain Admin, or a known directory-synchronization service account (e.g. Azure AD Connect). This is the specific ACL-grant precondition for a DCSync attack and is intentionally kept as a separate detection from actual replication use (see AD-REPL) per the requirement to treat rights-grant and rights-use as distinct signals.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on nTSecurityDescriptor at the domain naming-context DN, ObjectType GUIDs 1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2 (Get-Changes) / 1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2 (Get-Changes-All).

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 on the domain-root DN where the new ACE grants either replication ObjectType GUID to a trustee not in dcsync_authorized_principals.csv.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="nTSecurityDescriptor"
| where match(Object_DN, "^DC=")
| search Attribute_Value="*1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2*" OR Attribute_Value="*1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2*"
| rex field=Attribute_Value "Trustee=(?<trustee>\S+)"
| lookup dcsync_authorized_principals.csv trustee OUTPUT is_authorized
| where isnull(is_authorized)
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, trustee
tuning_guidance: Maintain dcsync_authorized_principals.csv with all DCs, Domain/Enterprise Admins, and known sync tools (Azure AD Connect/Entra Connect service account, third-party IAM). Alert on all matches — this is one of the highest-priority detections in the entire AD catalogue.
investigation_steps: Resolve the trustee and determine how it obtained rights to modify the domain-root ACL.
Check whether a DCSync replication request has already occurred (correlate with the AD-REPL namespace).
Review for a broader ACL-abuse chain leading to this grant.
response_guidance: Remove the ACE immediately, treat as a near-certain precursor to full domain credential compromise, and follow domain-compromise incident response procedures (krbtgt double-reset should be considered).
author: Threat Detection Library

title: ACE Removed from a Privileged Object (Baseline Deviation)
description: Detects an expected ACE being removed from a Tier-0 object's DACL relative to a maintained baseline. While often benign cleanup, removal of expected monitoring-relevant or restrictive ACEs (e.g. an explicit Deny ACE) can be used to quietly loosen an object's effective permissions without adding a new, more-obviously-suspicious Allow ACE.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on nTSecurityDescriptor compared to adminsdholder_template.csv or a periodic ACL export baseline.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 on a Tier-0 object where the new ACE count/composition has fewer entries than the last known-good baseline snapshot.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="nTSecurityDescriptor"
| lookup tier0_objects.csv object_dn AS Object_DN OUTPUT is_tier0
| where is_tier0=1
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, Attribute_Value
| note "Compare Attribute_Value ACE set against the periodic ACL baseline export for this object_dn; flag any expected ACE missing from the new value."
tuning_guidance: Requires an out-of-band periodic ACL baseline export process (e.g. weekly dsacls/PowerShell export to a lookup) — this detection cannot function purely from streaming 5136 events without that baseline.
investigation_steps: Compare the full before/after ACE set.
Determine whether the removal was part of an approved cleanup or hardening change.
response_guidance: Restore the expected ACE if the removal was unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: GPO Object DACL Modified to Grant Edit Rights to Unexpected Principal
description: Detects a Group Policy Object's DACL being modified to grant write/edit rights to a principal not in the expected GPO-management group. Since GPOs can push arbitrary settings, scripts, and scheduled tasks to every computer they are linked to, gaining edit rights on a widely linked GPO is one of the most efficient fleet-wide persistence and lateral-movement mechanisms available in AD.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on nTSecurityDescriptor where Object_Class=groupPolicyContainer.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where Object_Class=groupPolicyContainer and the new ACE grants write rights to a trustee outside gpo_management_principals.csv.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="nTSecurityDescriptor" Object_Class=groupPolicyContainer
| rex field=Attribute_Value "Mask=(?<ace_mask>0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+).*Trustee=(?<trustee>\S+)"
| where ace_mask="0x10000000" OR ace_mask="0x40000000" OR ace_mask="0x40000"
| lookup gpo_management_principals.csv trustee OUTPUT is_expected
| where isnull(is_expected)
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, trustee, ace_mask
tuning_guidance: Cross-reference against gpo_link_scope.csv to prioritize GPOs linked at the domain root or DC OU (see AD-GPO namespace for link-scope detections).
investigation_steps: Determine the GPO's link scope — domain-root/DC-linked GPOs are Critical.
Review recent GPO content changes from the newly-privileged trustee.
response_guidance: Remove the unauthorized ACE and review the GPO's full settings for tampering.

references.title: Domain Policy Modification: Group Policy Modification

author: Threat Detection Library

title: OU Created with Unusual Delegated Permissions
description: Detects creation of a new Organizational Unit whose initial DACL grants rights beyond the organization's standard OU-delegation template. A newly created OU with broad rights delegated to a non-standard principal can serve as a staging area for objects the attacker fully controls (e.g. moving or creating computer/user accounts into it).

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5137 (OU created) and 5136 on the new OU's nTSecurityDescriptor.

detection_logic: Event ID 5137 (directory-service object created, objectClass=organizationalUnit) followed within 1 hour by a 5136 ACL change on the same DN granting non-standard rights.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5137 Object_Class=organizationalUnit
| join Object_DN [ search index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="nTSecurityDescriptor" | rename Object_DN as Object_DN ]
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN
tuning_guidance: Requires DS Access auditing for object creation (5137) in addition to attribute changes.
investigation_steps: Review the OU's purpose and confirm against change-management records.
Check what objects are subsequently created or moved into the new OU.
response_guidance: Review and tighten delegation if the OU does not match a documented purpose.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Organizational Unit Deleted
description: Detects deletion of an Organizational Unit. Because deleting an OU (when protection from accidental deletion is not set) can cascade-delete its contents, this can be both a destructive-attack indicator and an efficient way to hide the trace of previously staged objects.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5141 (directory-service object deleted, objectClass=organizationalUnit).

detection_logic: Event ID 5141 where Object_Class=organizationalUnit.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5141 Object_Class=organizationalUnit
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches for OUs containing Tier-0 objects; route others to a standard change-review queue.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a change ticket.
Check the AD Recycle Bin for the deleted OU's prior contents.
Review whether this coincides with other destructive activity (bulk user/group deletion).
response_guidance: Restore from the AD Recycle Bin if unauthorized and investigate as a potential destructive attack.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Deny ACE Removed from a Sensitive Object
description: Detects removal of an explicit Deny ACE from a Tier-0 object. Deny ACEs are sometimes used defensively to explicitly block a broad group (e.g. Domain Users) from an otherwise-inheritable right; removing one silently widens effective access without adding an obviously suspicious new Allow entry.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on nTSecurityDescriptor, comparing prior/new ACE lists for missing Deny (D;) entries.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 on a Tier-0 object where a baseline-known Deny ACE (D; prefix in SDDL) is absent from the new Attribute_Value.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="nTSecurityDescriptor"
| lookup tier0_objects.csv object_dn AS Object_DN OUTPUT is_tier0
| where is_tier0=1
| lookup adminsdholder_template.csv object_dn AS Object_DN OUTPUT expected_deny_aces
| where isnotnull(expected_deny_aces) AND NOT like(Attribute_Value, "%".expected_deny_aces."%")
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained per-object baseline of expected Deny ACEs; this is a niche, low-frequency but high-value check once baselined.
investigation_steps: Confirm the removal against a documented ACL change.
Assess what access the removal effectively grants to the previously-denied group.
response_guidance: Restore the Deny ACE if unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Self-Membership (Self) Right Granted on a Privileged Group
description: Detects the Self-Membership extended right (which allows a trustee to add itself to a group) being granted on a Tier-0 group such as Domain Admins. This right is narrowly scoped but extremely dangerous — it lets the trustee join the privileged group directly without needing any other write access to the group object.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on nTSecurityDescriptor, ObjectType GUID bf9679c0-0de6-11d0-a285-00aa003049e2 (Self-Membership).

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where the new ACE ObjectType matches the Self-Membership GUID on a Tier-0 group.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="nTSecurityDescriptor"
| lookup tier0_privileged_groups.csv object_dn AS Object_DN OUTPUT is_tier0_group
| where is_tier0_group=1
| search Attribute_Value="*bf9679c0-0de6-11d0-a285-00aa003049e2*"
| rex field=Attribute_Value "Trustee=(?<trustee>\S+)"
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, trustee
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches; there is essentially no legitimate reason to grant Self-Membership on Domain Admins/Enterprise Admins to a non-administrative principal.
investigation_steps: Resolve trustee and check whether it has already added itself to the group (correlate with AD-GRP-001/003/004).
Determine how the granting actor obtained rights to modify the group ACL.
response_guidance: Remove the ACE immediately and remove the trustee from the group if it has already joined.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Bulk ACL Modification Across Many Objects by a Single Actor
description: Detects a single actor modifying the DACL of an unusually large number of distinct AD objects within a short window — a pattern consistent with an automated ACL-abuse tool (e.g. a scripted BloodHound-driven attack) sweeping many objects to plant multiple redundant persistence paths at once.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on nTSecurityDescriptor grouped by actor.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 on nTSecurityDescriptor grouped by Subject_Account_Name over 1 hour; alert when distinct_count(Object_DN) >= 10.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="nTSecurityDescriptor"
| bucket _time span=1h
| stats dc(Object_DN) as objects_modified values(Object_DN) as objects by _time, Subject_Account_Name
| where objects_modified >= 10
tuning_guidance: Exclude known bulk-provisioning/onboarding scripts and identity-governance tooling via authorized_identity_admins.csv.
investigation_steps: Review the full list of modified objects for privileged-object overlap.
Determine whether this reflects a legitimate bulk-delegation project or an attack.
response_guidance: If unauthorized, treat as an active large-scale persistence-planting event; audit every modified object's new ACL for unexpected grants.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: ACL Modification on a Certificate Template Object
description: Detects a DACL change on an AD CS certificate-template object granting enrollment or write rights to an unexpected principal. Certificate-template ACL abuse (ESC4-style attacks) lets an attacker modify a template's own properties (e.g. enabling client-authentication EKU or disabling manager approval) to create a new certificate-based privilege-escalation path, or grants enrollment rights that allow requesting certificates usable for domain authentication.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on nTSecurityDescriptor for objects under the Certificate Templates container.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where Object_DN is under CN=Certificate Templates,CN=Public Key Services,CN=Services,CN=Configuration and the new ACE grants write/enroll rights to a trustee outside pki_management_principals.csv.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="nTSecurityDescriptor"
| where match(Object_DN, "CN=Certificate Templates,CN=Public Key Services,CN=Services,CN=Configuration")
| rex field=Attribute_Value "Mask=(?<ace_mask>0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+).*Trustee=(?<trustee>\S+)"
| lookup pki_management_principals.csv trustee OUTPUT is_expected
| where isnull(is_expected)
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, trustee, ace_mask
tuning_guidance: This detection targets the ACL-abuse half of AD CS attack paths (ESC4); template-property changes themselves (EKU/manager-approval flags) should be tracked as a companion detection in a future AD CS-focused batch. Alert on all matches for templates that are also flagged high-privilege in a certificate-template inventory.
investigation_steps: Review the specific template and its current EKU/issuance settings.
Check whether certificates have since been requested using the template by unusual principals.
response_guidance: Revert the ACL change; if a certificate was already issued via the abused template, revoke it and investigate the requesting principal.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: ACL Modification on the AdminSDHolder Container Itself (Not via SDProp)
description: Detects a direct DACL modification of the AdminSDHolder container object (CN=AdminSDHolder,CN=System,<domain-DN>) rather than of an object protected by it. Because SDProp copies AdminSDHolder's ACL onto every protected privileged object roughly every 60 minutes, an attacker who successfully modifies AdminSDHolder's own ACL gains a single, durable change that silently persists across every current and future Tier-0 object — this is considered one of the highest-leverage single actions possible in the entire domain.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 where Object_DN is exactly the AdminSDHolder container DN.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where Object_DN matches 'CN=AdminSDHolder,CN=System,<domain-DN>' exactly.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="nTSecurityDescriptor"
| where match(Object_DN, "^CN=AdminSDHolder,CN=System,DC=")
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, Attribute_Value
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches without exception — this is a near-zero-frequency event in a healthy domain and duplicates/overlaps with AD-GRP-013/014/015 (kept here as well because ACL analysts specifically monitor this container separately from group-membership analysts).
investigation_steps: Immediately capture the full before/after ACE set.
Identify the actor and their authorization to modify this object.
Assume the change has already propagated to every protected object via the next SDProp cycle (~60 minutes) if not caught immediately.
response_guidance: Revert the AdminSDHolder ACL to its known-good baseline immediately, then verify (and manually correct if needed) every protected object's ACL rather than waiting for the next SDProp cycle to fix them.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: ACL Change Grants Rights Across a Trust Boundary
description: Detects a DACL change on a Tier-0 object in the local domain that grants rights to a security principal whose SID belongs to a foreign domain or forest reachable via an established trust. Cross-trust ACL grants can be used to extend a compromise from a smaller, less-defended trusted domain into rights over the primary domain's most sensitive objects.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on nTSecurityDescriptor where the trustee SID's domain portion does not match the local domain SID.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 on a Tier-0 object where the new ACE's trustee SID prefix matches a known trusted-domain SID rather than the local domain SID.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="nTSecurityDescriptor"
| lookup tier0_objects.csv object_dn AS Object_DN OUTPUT is_tier0
| where is_tier0=1
| rex field=Attribute_Value "Trustee=(?<trustee_sid>S-1-5-21-\d+-\d+-\d+)"
| lookup trusted_domain_sids.csv domain_sid_prefix AS trustee_sid OUTPUT trusted_domain_name
| lookup local_domain_sid.csv domain_sid_prefix AS trustee_sid OUTPUT is_local
| where isnotnull(trusted_domain_name) AND isnull(is_local)
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, trustee_sid, trusted_domain_name
tuning_guidance: Requires maintaining trusted_domain_sids.csv and local_domain_sid.csv; this is a specialized detection best run as a scheduled report rather than real-time given SID-prefix parsing cost. Alert on all matches.
investigation_steps: Identify the trusted domain and its own security posture.
Determine whether this grant is part of an approved cross-forest administrative delegation.
Escalate to the trust-relationship owner if unapproved.
response_guidance: Remove the cross-trust ACE if unauthorized; review the trust's overall SID-filtering configuration (see AD-TRUST namespace).
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New Group Policy Object Created
description: Detects creation of a new GPO. GPO creation is routine in a managed environment, but every new GPO is a potential fleet-wide persistence and configuration-push mechanism once linked, so creation events are tracked as a baseline for correlation with subsequent linking and content changes.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5137 where Object_Class=groupPolicyContainer.

detection_logic: Event ID 5137 where Object_Class=groupPolicyContainer.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5137 Object_Class=groupPolicyContainer
| lookup gpo_management_principals.csv Subject_Account_Name OUTPUT is_expected
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, is_expected
tuning_guidance: Low-priority on its own; primarily useful as a building block for AD-GPO-002/010 chains and to seed a GPO inventory baseline.
investigation_steps: Confirm the creator is an expected GPO administrator.
Track the new GPO through to its first link event.
response_guidance: Not independently actionable; monitor for follow-on linking activity.

references.title: Domain Policy Modification: Group Policy Modification

author: Threat Detection Library

title: GPO Created by Unusual Actor Outside GPO-Management Group
description: Detects a new GPO created by a principal who is not a member of a recognized GPO-management group (e.g. Group Policy Creator Owners or a delegated GPO-admin group). Unauthorized GPO creation is a strong indicator that a compromised account with unexpected delegated rights, or one that has abused ACL/delegation paths, is staging a fleet-wide persistence or lateral-movement mechanism.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5137 where Object_Class=groupPolicyContainer.

detection_logic: Event ID 5137 (GPO created) where Subject_Account_Name is not in gpo_management_principals.csv.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5137 Object_Class=groupPolicyContainer
| lookup gpo_management_principals.csv Subject_Account_Name OUTPUT is_expected
| where isnull(is_expected)
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN
tuning_guidance: Maintain gpo_management_principals.csv accurately; alert on all matches.
investigation_steps: Determine how the actor obtained GPO-creation rights.
Review the GPO's initial content and link scope as soon as it appears.
response_guidance: Disable/unlink the GPO pending review and investigate the actor's broader activity for an ACL-abuse chain.

references.title: Domain Policy Modification: Group Policy Modification

author: Threat Detection Library

title: GPO Linked to Domain Controllers OU
description: Detects a GPO being linked to the Domain Controllers OU. Any GPO applied to the DC OU runs with SYSTEM-level effect on every domain controller, making this one of the highest-impact single actions possible in AD — a malicious GPO linked here can push a scheduled task, script, or registry change that executes as SYSTEM on every DC in the domain.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on gPLink attribute of the Domain Controllers OU.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name=gPLink and Object_DN is the Domain Controllers OU DN.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="gPLink"
| where match(Object_DN, "^OU=Domain Controllers,DC=")
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, Attribute_Value
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches without exception; DC-OU GPO links should change extremely rarely and only through a documented change process.
investigation_steps: Identify the exact GPO(s) now linked and review their full content immediately.
Confirm against a documented change ticket.
Check whether the GPO contains scheduled tasks, scripts, or registry changes.
response_guidance: Unlink the GPO immediately if unapproved and treat as an active domain-compromise indicator; assume every DC may have already applied the policy.

references.title: Domain Policy Modification: Group Policy Modification

author: Threat Detection Library

title: GPO Linked to Domain Root
description: Detects a GPO being linked at the domain root, which applies the policy to every computer and user in the domain by default (subject to inheritance/filtering). A malicious GPO linked at this scope is the single most efficient fleet-wide compromise mechanism available in AD.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on gPLink attribute of the domain-root DN.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name=gPLink and Object_DN equals the domain-root DN.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="gPLink"
| where match(Object_DN, "^DC=[^,]+,DC=[^,]+$")
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, Attribute_Value
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches; domain-root GPO links change infrequently in mature environments.
investigation_steps: Identify the linked GPO and review its full content immediately.
Confirm against change management.
Assess the number of computers/users the new link now affects.
response_guidance: Unlink immediately if unapproved; treat as a fleet-wide compromise event and audit endpoints for evidence of applied malicious policy.

references.title: Domain Policy Modification: Group Policy Modification

author: Threat Detection Library

title: GPO Security Filtering Modified
description: Detects a change to a GPO's security filtering (the Apply Group Policy ACE on the GPO itself). Narrowing security filtering to target only specific high-value computers/users — rather than widening it — is a common technique for a malicious GPO to affect only its intended targets (e.g. Tier-0 systems) while staying beneath fleet-wide anomaly-detection thresholds.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on nTSecurityDescriptor for a groupPolicyContainer object, ACE granting/denying Apply-Group-Policy.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 on a groupPolicyContainer object's nTSecurityDescriptor where the ACE's ObjectType matches the Apply-Group-Policy extended right GUID (edacfd8f-ffb3-11d1-b41d-00a0c968f939).
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="nTSecurityDescriptor" Object_Class=groupPolicyContainer
| search Attribute_Value="*edacfd8f-ffb3-11d1-b41d-00a0c968f939*"
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, Attribute_Value
tuning_guidance: Correlate with AD-GPO-003/004 for link-scope context; a security-filtering change on a widely linked GPO targeting Tier-0 systems specifically should be treated as high priority.
investigation_steps: Identify the new filtering scope and whether it now targets Tier-0 assets.
Review the GPO's content for anything newly relevant to that scope.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized filtering changes and review the GPO's full content.

references.title: Domain Policy Modification: Group Policy Modification

author: Threat Detection Library

title: GPO WMI Filter Changed to Target Specific Systems
description: Detects a change to a GPO's WMI filter linkage. Like security filtering, WMI filters can be used to scope a malicious GPO's application to a narrow, specific set of systems (e.g. by OS build or hostname pattern) while the GPO itself remains linked broadly, complicating detection based on link scope alone.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on gPCWQLFilter attribute of a groupPolicyContainer object.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name=gPCWQLFilter.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="gPCWQLFilter"
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, Attribute_Value
tuning_guidance: Low frequency in most environments; review each occurrence manually rather than tuning thresholds.
investigation_steps: Review the new WQL filter query for suspicious scoping (e.g. filtering to a specific small set of hostnames).
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.

references.title: Domain Policy Modification: Group Policy Modification

author: Threat Detection Library

title: GPO Modified to Add Scheduled Task (Group Policy Preferences)
description: Detects a change to a GPO's SYSVOL content indicating a new Scheduled Task (Group Policy Preferences ScheduledTasks.xml) was added. GPP scheduled tasks are a classic fleet-wide execution mechanism, letting an attacker run an arbitrary command as SYSTEM or a specified account on every computer the GPO applies to at the next policy refresh.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: File-system auditing on \\<domain>\SYSVOL\...\ScheduledTasks\ScheduledTasks.xml, Event ID 4663.

detection_logic: Event ID 4663 (object access) on a file path matching '*\Preferences\ScheduledTasks\ScheduledTasks.xml' under the SYSVOL share, with a write access mask.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4663 Object_Name="*\\Preferences\\ScheduledTasks\\ScheduledTasks.xml"
| search Accesses="*WriteData*" OR Accesses="*AppendData*"
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_Name
tuning_guidance: Requires SACL-based file-system auditing enabled on the SYSVOL share, which is not on by default — flag this as a telemetry dependency to validate before relying on the detection. Alert on all matches for GPOs linked to Tier-0 scope.
investigation_steps: Retrieve and review the ScheduledTasks.xml content for the command/executable being pushed.
Identify the GPO's link scope to assess blast radius.
Check target endpoints for the scheduled task actually landing (EDR/Sysmon Task Scheduler event 4698).
response_guidance: Remove the malicious scheduled task from the GPO immediately, unlink the GPO if scope is unclear, and hunt across the fleet for the task's execution.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires SYSVOL file-system SACL auditing, which many environments do not enable by default; this is an explicit telemetry dependency, not an assumed default.

title: GPP cpassword Attribute Written to SYSVOL
description: Detects a file write to a Group Policy Preferences XML file containing a cpassword attribute. Despite Microsoft's 2014 patch removing this capability from the GPMC UI, cpassword values can still be manually placed in GPP XML and the AES key used to encrypt them is publicly documented, meaning any cpassword value found in SYSVOL is a trivially recoverable plaintext credential.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: File-system auditing Event ID 4663 on SYSVOL Preferences XML files.

detection_logic: Event ID 4663 write access on a Preferences XML file (Groups.xml, Services.xml, ScheduledTasks.xml, DataSources.xml, Drives.xml, Printers.xml) — flag for content review to check for a cpassword attribute.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4663 Object_Name="*\\Preferences\\*.xml"
| search Accesses="*WriteData*" OR Accesses="*AppendData*"
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_Name
| note "Correlate with a periodic SYSVOL content scan for the cpassword= attribute; the file-write event alone does not confirm a credential was embedded."
tuning_guidance: Best paired with a periodic out-of-band SYSVOL grep for 'cpassword="[^"]' to positively confirm exposure rather than relying on the write event alone. Requires SYSVOL SACL auditing.
investigation_steps: Retrieve the XML content and confirm whether cpassword is present and non-empty.
If present, decrypt using the public AES key to determine the exposed credential and rotate it immediately.
response_guidance: Remove the cpassword-bearing preference item immediately and rotate the exposed credential domain-wide if it was a shared/local-admin password.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: File-write telemetry alone cannot confirm cpassword content; a companion out-of-band content scan is required for positive confirmation, consistent with the rule against inventing telemetry Splunk does not have.

title: GPO Restricted Groups Setting Modified
description: Detects a change to a GPO's Restricted Groups configuration, which controls local group membership (most commonly local Administrators) on every computer the GPO applies to. Adding a domain account to a Restricted Groups policy targeting local Administrators is a fleet-wide local-admin-persistence mechanism.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: File-system auditing Event ID 4663 on GptTmpl.inf under a GPO's SYSVOL Machine\Microsoft\Windows NT\SecEdit path.

detection_logic: Event ID 4663 write access on GptTmpl.inf paths under a GPO's SYSVOL folder.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4663 Object_Name="*\\SecEdit\\GptTmpl.inf"
| search Accesses="*WriteData*" OR Accesses="*AppendData*"
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_Name
tuning_guidance: Requires SYSVOL SACL auditing. Correlate with the GPO's link scope; a Restricted Groups change on a broadly-linked GPO is high priority.
investigation_steps: Retrieve the GptTmpl.inf content and identify which accounts were added to which local groups.
Determine the GPO's link scope to assess how many computers are affected.
response_guidance: Revert the unauthorized Restricted Groups change and audit affected computers' actual local group membership for drift.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New GPO Created and Linked to Fleet-Wide Scope Within Short Window (Chain)
description: The flagship GPO-abuse chain: a new GPO is created and then linked to a broad scope (domain root or Domain Controllers OU) within a short window, consistent with an attacker rapidly staging and deploying a malicious policy before defenders can react. Legitimate GPO rollouts are typically tested in a narrow pilot scope first, making immediate broad linkage of a brand-new GPO itself suspicious independent of content.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5137 (GPO created) and 5136 (gPLink change to broad scope) correlated by actor within a short window.

detection_logic: AD-GPO-001 (GPO created) followed within 2 hours by a gPLink change linking the same GPO GUID at domain-root or Domain-Controllers-OU scope (AD-GPO-003/004 match) from the same actor.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" (EventCode=5137 OR (EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="gPLink"))
| eval etype=if(EventCode=5137, "gpo_created", "gpo_linked")
| eval is_broad_scope=if(etype="gpo_linked" AND (match(Object_DN,"^OU=Domain Controllers,DC=") OR match(Object_DN,"^DC=[^,]+,DC=[^,]+$")), 1, 0)
| transaction Subject_Account_Name maxspan=2h startswith=eval(etype="gpo_created") endswith=eval(is_broad_scope=1)
| where eventcount=2
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, duration
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches; suppress only for a documented emergency-change process with pre-authorization.
investigation_steps: Immediately retrieve the full content of the newly linked GPO.
Assume fleet-wide policy application has begun and check endpoint telemetry for the pushed configuration.
response_guidance: Unlink and disable the GPO immediately; this is treated as an active fleet-wide compromise attempt pending validation.

references.title: Domain Policy Modification: Group Policy Modification

author: Threat Detection Library

title: GPO Deleted
description: Detects deletion of a GPO. While routine during cleanup, deletion of a GPO linked to sensitive scope, or deletion shortly after suspicious content changes, can indicate an attacker removing evidence of a malicious policy after it has already applied to its targets.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5141 where Object_Class=groupPolicyContainer.

detection_logic: Event ID 5141 where Object_Class=groupPolicyContainer.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5141 Object_Class=groupPolicyContainer
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN
tuning_guidance: Escalate priority if the deleted GPO was recently linked to broad scope (correlate with AD-GPO-003/004/010) or recently modified (AD-GPO-007/008/009).
investigation_steps: Check the AD Recycle Bin / SYSVOL backup for the deleted GPO's last content.
Determine what the GPO applied before deletion and whether targets already received it.
response_guidance: Restore from backup if investigation is needed; audit affected endpoints for lingering effects of the deleted policy.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: GPO Enforced Flag Set on Sensitive-Scope Link
description: Detects a GPO link's Enforced (No Override) flag being set. An enforced GPO link cannot be blocked by inheritance-blocking at lower OUs, guaranteeing a malicious policy applies regardless of downstream block-inheritance settings — useful to an attacker who wants to guarantee application to a specific OU despite existing defensive GPO precedence.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on gPOptions/gPLink flags.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 on gPLink where the link options flag changes to include the Enforced bit (LDAP_REF flag 2).
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="gPLink"
| rex field=Attribute_Value "\[LDAP://(?<gpo_dn>[^;]+);(?<link_flags>\d+)\]"
| where link_flags=2 OR link_flags=3
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, gpo_dn, link_flags
tuning_guidance: Low-frequency event in most environments; review manually.
investigation_steps: Identify the GPO and its content.
Determine why enforcement was needed.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized.

references.title: Domain Policy Modification: Group Policy Modification

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Block Inheritance Toggled on a Sensitive OU
description: Detects the Block Policy Inheritance flag being toggled on an OU. Enabling block-inheritance on an OU containing sensitive systems can be used to prevent a domain-wide defensive/monitoring GPO from applying to those systems, effectively carving out an exemption for attacker-controlled or attacker-targeted assets.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on gPOptions attribute of an OU object.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name=gPOptions and Attribute_Value=1 (block inheritance enabled) on an OU object.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="gPOptions" Object_Class=organizationalUnit
| where Attribute_Value="1"
| lookup tier0_ous.csv target_ou AS Object_DN OUTPUT is_tier0_ou
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, is_tier0_ou
tuning_guidance: Treat is_tier0_ou=1 matches as high priority; otherwise route to standard change review.
investigation_steps: Determine which domain-wide GPOs would have applied to this OU absent the block.
Confirm against a documented change.
response_guidance: Revert if unauthorized, particularly for OUs containing monitored/Tier-0 systems.

references.title: Domain Policy Modification: Group Policy Modification

author: Threat Detection Library

title: GPO Modifies Windows Defender / Antivirus Exclusions or Disablement
description: Detects a GPO whose SYSVOL Registry.pol content includes a change disabling Windows Defender/AV real-time protection or adding broad exclusion paths. Deploying this via GPO is an efficient way to blind an entire fleet segment ahead of malware deployment or credential-dumping activity.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: File-system auditing Event ID 4663 on Registry.pol for a GPO's Machine\Microsoft\Windows NT\SecEdit or Machine policy path.

detection_logic: Event ID 4663 write access on Registry.pol under a GPO's Machine folder, flagged for content review against known Defender-disablement registry keys.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4663 Object_Name="*\\Machine\\Registry.pol"
| search Accesses="*WriteData*" OR Accesses="*AppendData*"
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_Name
| note "Correlate with a periodic Registry.pol content scan for DisableAntiSpyware, DisableRealtimeMonitoring, or broad Exclusions paths."
tuning_guidance: Requires SYSVOL SACL auditing plus a companion content-scan process; the write event alone cannot confirm Defender-disabling content.
investigation_steps: Retrieve and review the Registry.pol content for Defender-related keys.
Identify the GPO's link scope.
Check affected endpoints for Defender status drift.
response_guidance: Revert the GPO content immediately and re-enable Defender across affected endpoints; treat as a probable pre-malware-deployment step.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires SYSVOL SACL auditing plus content inspection; file-write telemetry alone does not confirm the specific registry keys changed.

title: GPO Modifies Windows Firewall Rules
description: Detects a GPO change to Windows Firewall rules content, which can be used to open inbound ports (e.g. RDP, SMB, WinRM) fleet-wide to facilitate lateral movement, or to disable the firewall outright on targeted systems.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: File-system auditing Event ID 4663 on a GPO's firewall policy files (WFAS registry.pol or GPFW template).

detection_logic: Event ID 4663 write access on GPO firewall-policy content paths.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4663 Object_Name="*\\Machine\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\SecEdit\\GptTmpl.inf"
| search Accesses="*WriteData*" OR Accesses="*AppendData*"
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_Name
tuning_guidance: Requires SYSVOL SACL auditing; correlate with the GPO's link scope for prioritization.
investigation_steps: Review the firewall rule changes for newly opened inbound ports.
Check for a subsequent lateral-movement attempt targeting the newly opened port on affected endpoints.
response_guidance: Revert unauthorized firewall changes and audit for exploitation of the newly opened access.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: GPO Modifies Audit Policy (Fleet-Wide Logging Impairment)
description: Detects a GPO change to the Advanced Audit Policy configuration (audit.csv within the GPO's SYSVOL content), which controls which security events are logged fleet-wide. An attacker reducing audit scope via GPO is a high-leverage, fleet-wide defense-evasion move that silences telemetry collection at the source rather than tampering with individual endpoints or the SIEM pipeline.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: File-system auditing Event ID 4663 on a GPO's audit.csv.

detection_logic: Event ID 4663 write access on '*\Microsoft\Windows NT\Audit\audit.csv' under a GPO's SYSVOL folder.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4663 Object_Name="*\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\Audit\\audit.csv"
| search Accesses="*WriteData*" OR Accesses="*AppendData*"
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_Name
tuning_guidance: Requires SYSVOL SACL auditing. Alert on all matches for GPOs linked to Domain Controllers or domain root.
investigation_steps: Retrieve the audit.csv content and compare against the expected audit-policy baseline.
Identify what categories were reduced and the GPO's link scope.
response_guidance: Revert immediately and treat as a likely precursor to further undetected malicious activity; increase manual review of affected systems until logging is confirmed restored.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: GPO Version Number Mismatch Between AD and SYSVOL (Tampering Indicator)
description: Each GPO tracks a version number in both its AD object (versionNumber attribute) and its SYSVOL GPT.INI file; these should always match. A mismatch indicates the SYSVOL content was modified directly (e.g. by an attacker with file-system access to SYSVOL bypassing the normal GPMC edit path) without the corresponding AD attribute being incremented, or vice versa — a known technique to modify GPO content while evading GPMC-based change review.

data_sources.name: ldapsearch
data_sources.description: Periodic comparison of AD versionNumber attribute against the SYSVOL GPT.INI Version value for every GPO.
