required_log_sources: Windows Directory Service Diagnostics Event Log

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Directory Service
data_sources.description: Directory Service diagnostics log, paged-search continuation events grouped by source.

detection_logic: Directory Service diagnostics search events with paging continuation from the same Client_IP_Address exceeding a page-count threshold within 30 minutes.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Directory Service" EventCode=1644
| bucket _time span=30m
| stats count as page_count by _time, Client_IP_Address, base_dn
| where page_count > 50 AND base_dn="*DC=*"
tuning_guidance: Requires the Field Engineering diagnostic logging level. Exclude known backup/directory-sync tooling (Azure AD Connect, identity-governance platforms) via a source allowlist.
investigation_steps: Identify the source and confirm whether it is an authorized sync/export process.
If unauthorized, treat as a large-scale directory-data exfiltration attempt.
response_guidance: Investigate the source and block if unauthorized; review what data may have already been exported.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires the Field Engineering (or equivalent expensive-search) diagnostic logging level on domain controllers.

title: LDAP Write Operation Immediately Following an NTLM-Relayed Bind
description: Detects an LDAP directory-service write operation (5136) occurring immediately after an unsigned LDAP bind (AD-LDAP-001) from a source that also matches a recent NTLM-relay-pattern indicator (AD-NTLM-007/008/009 from the AD-NTLM namespace). This combination is the specific signature of a successful NTLM-relay-to-LDAP attack resulting in an actual directory modification — for example, the relayed identity being used to grant itself DCSync rights or add itself to a privileged group.
required_log_sources: Windows Directory Service Diagnostics Event Log

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Directory Service
data_sources.description: Directory Service diagnostics log (unsigned bind) correlated with DC security event log (directory-service write) by source IP and timestamp.

detection_logic: AD-LDAP-001 (unsigned bind) from a source IP followed within 5 minutes by an Event ID 5136 directory-service write where the writing account's recent authentication pattern matches an NTLM-relay indicator from the same source IP.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Directory Service" EventCode=2889
| eval etype="unsigned_bind"
| append [
    search index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136
    | eval etype="ldap_write"
    | rename IpAddress as Client_IP_Address
  ]
| transaction Client_IP_Address maxspan=5m startswith=eval(etype="unsigned_bind") endswith=eval(etype="ldap_write")
| where eventcount=2
| table _time, dvc, Client_IP_Address, Object_DN, duration
tuning_guidance: This is a best-effort correlation given the difficulty of directly attributing an LDAP write to a specific unsigned-bind session from separate log sources; treat as a supporting indicator alongside AD-COMP-006 and AD-ACL findings rather than a fully self-contained detection.
investigation_steps: Identify exactly what directory change was made.
Cross-reference with AD-COMP-006 (DC coerced outbound) and any AD-ACL findings for the same time window.
Assume a successful relay-based directory compromise if the write granted sensitive rights.
response_guidance: Treat as an active, likely successful NTLM-relay-to-LDAP attack; revert the directory change, enforce LDAP signing/channel binding immediately, and remediate the coercion vector.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Correlating an LDAP write to a specific relayed bind session across separate log sources (Directory Service diagnostics and Security event log) is inherently approximate without a shared session identifier; treat this as a supporting, not conclusive, indicator.

title: LDAP Query for gMSA/LAPS Managed-Password Attributes at Scale
description: Detects an LDAP search filter or attribute-selection list requesting msDS-ManagedPassword (gMSA) or ms-Mcs-AdmPwd/msLAPS-Password (LAPS) attributes across many objects from a single source. This is a broader, LDAP-query-level companion to the AD-LAPS namespace's access-event detections, catching the reconnaissance/enumeration phase where an attacker identifies which objects it can successfully request these secrets from before actually retrieving them at scale.
required_log_sources: Windows Directory Service Diagnostics Event Log

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Directory Service
data_sources.description: Directory Service diagnostics log, search events with attribute-selection lists including msDS-ManagedPassword or ms-Mcs-AdmPwd/msLAPS-Password across multiple objects.

detection_logic: Directory Service diagnostics search events where attributes_requested includes msDS-ManagedPassword or ms-Mcs-AdmPwd/msLAPS-Password, grouped by source, where distinct object count exceeds a small threshold within 15 minutes.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Directory Service" EventCode=1644
| search attributes_requested="*msDS-ManagedPassword*" OR attributes_requested="*ms-Mcs-AdmPwd*" OR attributes_requested="*msLAPS-Password*"
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats dc(Object_DN) as objects_queried by _time, Client_IP_Address
| where objects_queried >= 5
tuning_guidance: Requires the Field Engineering diagnostic logging level with attribute-selection-list capture. Exclude known LAPS/gMSA-management tooling and PAM platforms via a source allowlist.
investigation_steps: Identify the source and account.
Correlate with the AD-LAPS namespace's actual secret-retrieval events for the same source to assess whether the reconnaissance converted to actual access.
response_guidance: Treat as an active credential-harvesting reconnaissance phase; investigate the source and tighten read-access delegation on these attributes if the source is unauthorized.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires the Field Engineering (or equivalent expensive-search) diagnostic logging level with attribute-selection-list visibility, which is a non-default and relatively verbose logging configuration.

title: LDAP Server Signing/Channel Binding Requirement Weakened
description: Detects the domain-wide LDAPServerIntegrity or LdapEnforceChannelBinding registry policy being changed to a weaker enforcement level on a domain controller. Weakening either setting re-opens the NTLM-relay-to-LDAP attack surface that signing/channel-binding enforcement is specifically designed to close, and doing so is a plausible pre-step before conducting a relay attack.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 4657 on the LDAPServerIntegrity or LdapEnforceChannelBinding registry values.

detection_logic: Event ID 4657 on HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\NTDS\Parameters\LDAPServerIntegrity or \LdapEnforceChannelBinding where New_Value is numerically lower (weaker) than Old_Value.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4657 (Object_Name="*NTDS\\Parameters\\LDAPServerIntegrity" OR Object_Name="*NTDS\\Parameters\\LdapEnforceChannelBinding")
| where tonumber(New_Value) < tonumber(Old_Value)
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_Name, Old_Value, New_Value
tuning_guidance: Requires registry SACL auditing on these specific keys. Alert on all matches without exception.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification (should be rare — typically only during a documented legacy-compatibility exception).
Restore the stronger enforcement level as soon as the exception is no longer needed.
response_guidance: Revert immediately unless a documented, time-boxed exception is in effect; treat any period of weakened enforcement as an elevated NTLM-relay risk window.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: LDAP Bind Using an Expired or Disabled Account Credential
description: Detects an LDAP simple bind attempt using credentials for an account that is currently disabled or has an expired password. A successful bind under these conditions should not occur, but a pattern of repeated attempts against a disabled account via LDAP (bypassing the Kerberos pre-authentication check that would normally surface this via 4768/0x12 failure codes) can indicate an attacker testing captured but stale credentials.
required_log_sources: Windows Directory Service Diagnostics Event Log

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Directory Service
data_sources.description: Directory Service diagnostics log, Event ID 2889 correlated with the target account's current enabled/expired state via a periodic account-status lookup.

detection_logic: Event ID 2889 where bind_account is present in disabled_accounts.csv.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Directory Service" EventCode=2889
| lookup disabled_accounts.csv account AS bind_account OUTPUT is_disabled
| where is_disabled=1
| table _time, dvc, Client_IP_Address, bind_account
tuning_guidance: Requires the LDAP Interface Events diagnostic logging level and a maintained disabled_accounts.csv baseline.
investigation_steps: Identify the source and confirm the account's disabled status is intentional.
Assess whether the credential material may be part of a broader compromised-credential set.
response_guidance: Investigate the source; not independently high-urgency but worth tracking alongside AD-AUTH-012's Kerberos/NTLM-based equivalent.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires the LDAP Interface Events diagnostic logging level on domain controllers.

title: LAPS Password Attribute Read by an Unauthorized Principal
description: Detects a read of the ms-Mcs-AdmPwd (legacy LAPS) or msLAPS-Password (Windows LAPS) attribute by a principal not present in the maintained list of authorized LAPS readers (typically a small, tightly scoped helpdesk/PAM group). LAPS stores each computer's local Administrator password in plaintext-equivalent form in this attribute; any unauthorized read is equivalent to direct local-administrator credential theft for that computer.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 4662 with Properties containing the ms-Mcs-AdmPwd or msLAPS-Password attribute GUID.

detection_logic: Event ID 4662 where Properties includes the ms-Mcs-AdmPwd (GUID 4c164200-20c0-11d0-a768-00aa006e0529's ms-Mcs-AdmPwd extension) or msLAPS-Password attribute, and Subject_Account_Name is not in authorized_laps_readers.csv.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4662
| search Properties="*ms-Mcs-AdmPwd*" OR Properties="*msLAPS-Password*"
| lookup authorized_laps_readers.csv Subject_Account_Name OUTPUT is_authorized
| where isnull(is_authorized)
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_Name
tuning_guidance: Requires DS Access auditing with object-access auditing configured on the LAPS attributes specifically (a SACL must be placed on the attribute, which is not automatic). Maintain authorized_laps_readers.csv tightly — this should typically be a very small, PAM-integrated group.
investigation_steps: Resolve the reading account and confirm it lacks legitimate LAPS-read delegation.
Identify the target computer and treat its local Administrator password as compromised.
Check for subsequent local-admin authentication to that computer.
response_guidance: Rotate the target computer's local Administrator password immediately (LAPS supports on-demand rotation) and investigate the reading account's access path.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Bulk LAPS Password Reads Across Many Computers by a Single Actor
description: The flagship LAPS-abuse detection: detects a single actor reading LAPS password attributes across an unusually large number of distinct computer objects within a short window. Because LAPS is deployed precisely to make local-admin passwords unique per machine and centrally protected, a bulk read across many machines defeats that protection at once and hands an attacker local-administrator access to a large swath of the fleet — this is a near-complete lateral-movement enabler if successful.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 4662 LAPS attribute reads grouped by actor.

detection_logic: Event ID 4662 where Properties includes the LAPS attribute GUID, grouped by Subject_Account_Name over 30 minutes; alert when distinct_count(Object_Name) >= 10.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4662
| search Properties="*ms-Mcs-AdmPwd*" OR Properties="*msLAPS-Password*"
| bucket _time span=30m
| stats dc(Object_Name) as computers_read values(Object_Name) as computers by _time, Subject_Account_Name
| where computers_read >= 10
tuning_guidance: Requires DS Access auditing scoped to the LAPS attribute SACL. Exclude known PAM/vaulting platforms that legitimately perform bulk rotation-verification reads, via authorized_laps_readers.csv.
investigation_steps: Treat as an active, large-scale lateral-movement enablement event.
Identify every computer whose password was read and rotate all of them immediately.
Investigate the actor's initial access and how it obtained bulk LAPS-read rights.
response_guidance: Rotate LAPS passwords for every affected computer immediately, treat as a fleet-wide credential-compromise incident, and investigate/remove the actor's LAPS-read delegation.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: LAPS Read Delegation (ExtendedRight) Granted to an Unexpected Principal
description: Detects an ACE granting the extended right to read the LAPS password attribute (or the CONTROL_ACCESS right for AllowedToRetrieveManagedPassword-equivalent LAPS read delegation) being added for a principal outside the expected LAPS-management group. This is the rights-grant precursor to AD-LAPS-001/002 and, per the pattern established for DCSync and delegation rights, is tracked as a separate signal from the actual read.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on nTSecurityDescriptor for a computer object, ACE referencing the ms-Mcs-AdmPwd/msLAPS-Password attribute or its associated confidential-attribute control-access right.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 on nTSecurityDescriptor where the new ACE's ObjectType references the LAPS password attribute GUID, and the trustee is not in authorized_laps_readers.csv.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="nTSecurityDescriptor"
| search Attribute_Value="*ms-Mcs-AdmPwd*" OR Attribute_Value="*msLAPS-Password*"
| rex field=Attribute_Value "Trustee=(?<trustee>\S+)"
| lookup authorized_laps_readers.csv trustee OUTPUT is_authorized
| where isnull(is_authorized)
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, trustee
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches without exception.
investigation_steps: Resolve the trustee and determine how the granting actor obtained rights to modify this ACL.
Check for an immediate subsequent read (correlate AD-LAPS-001/002).
response_guidance: Remove the unauthorized ACE immediately and rotate the affected computer's LAPS password as a precaution.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: gMSA Managed Password Attribute Read by an Unauthorized Principal
description: Detects a read of a Group Managed Service Account's msDS-ManagedPassword attribute by a principal not listed in that gMSA's own PrincipalsAllowedToRetrieveManagedPassword configuration. gMSA passwords are automatically rotated, complex, and centrally managed specifically to eliminate static service-account credential exposure; a read by an unauthorized principal defeats that protection and hands the attacker the service account's current live credential.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 4662 with Properties containing the msDS-ManagedPassword attribute.

detection_logic: Event ID 4662 where Properties includes msDS-ManagedPassword, and Subject_Account_Name is not present in the target gMSA's authorized retrieval list (via gmsa_authorized_retrievers.csv).
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4662
| search Properties="*msDS-ManagedPassword*"
| lookup gmsa_authorized_retrievers.csv Object_Name, Subject_Account_Name OUTPUT is_authorized
| where isnull(is_authorized)
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_Name
tuning_guidance: Requires DS Access auditing on gMSA objects. Maintain gmsa_authorized_retrievers.csv reflecting each gMSA's actual PrincipalsAllowedToRetrieveManagedPassword configuration.
investigation_steps: Resolve the reading account and confirm it is not on the gMSA's approved retrieval list.
Treat the gMSA's current password as compromised.
Check for subsequent authentication as the gMSA from an unexpected source.
response_guidance: Investigate the reading account's access path (this typically indicates the account was itself added to PrincipalsAllowedToRetrieveManagedPassword improperly — correlate AD-LAPS-005); rotate/restrict as needed.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: gMSA PrincipalsAllowedToRetrieveManagedPassword Modified
description: Detects a gMSA's msDS-GroupMSAMembership (PrincipalsAllowedToRetrieveManagedPassword) attribute being modified to add a new principal. This is the specific rights-grant precursor to AD-LAPS-004 and controls exactly which computers/accounts are permitted to retrieve the gMSA's live password — any addition outside a documented service-deployment change warrants review.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on msDS-GroupMSAMembership.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name=msDS-GroupMSAMembership.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="msDS-GroupMSAMembership"
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, Attribute_Value
tuning_guidance: Maintain authorized_identity_admins.csv/service-deployment-tooling allowlist for expected changes; alert on all matches for gMSAs flagged high-value in high_value_service_accounts.csv.
investigation_steps: Identify the added principal and confirm business justification.
Check for an immediate subsequent managed-password read from the newly added principal (correlate AD-LAPS-004).
response_guidance: Remove the unauthorized principal from the retrieval list immediately.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New gMSA Account Created
description: Detects creation of a new Group Managed Service Account. gMSA creation itself is routine, but each new gMSA is a new object with its own retrieval delegation to track; this detection establishes a baseline for correlation with the retrieval-delegation and read-access detections elsewhere in this namespace.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5137 where Object_Class=msDS-GroupManagedServiceAccount.

detection_logic: Event ID 5137 where Object_Class=msDS-GroupManagedServiceAccount.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5137 Object_Class=msDS-GroupManagedServiceAccount
| lookup authorized_identity_admins.csv Subject_Account_Name OUTPUT is_expected
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, is_expected
tuning_guidance: Low priority on its own; escalate if the creator is unexpected or if the new gMSA's initial retrieval delegation (correlate AD-LAPS-005) is unusually broad.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification.
Review the initial PrincipalsAllowedToRetrieveManagedPassword configuration.
response_guidance: Not independently actionable; track for baseline purposes.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: LAPS Password Expiration Timestamp Manipulated
description: Detects the ms-Mcs-AdmPwdExpirationTime attribute being modified to a far-future value. Setting an artificially distant expiration time delays the automatic rotation of a computer's LAPS-managed local Administrator password, extending the useful lifetime of a credential an attacker may have already obtained via AD-LAPS-001/002.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on ms-Mcs-AdmPwdExpirationTime.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name=ms-Mcs-AdmPwdExpirationTime and the new value is more than 90 days in the future.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="ms-Mcs-AdmPwdExpirationTime"
| eval expiration_epoch=(tonumber(Attribute_Value)/10000000)-11644473600
| eval days_out=round((expiration_epoch-now())/86400)
| where days_out > 90
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, days_out
tuning_guidance: Correlate with a recent AD-LAPS-001/002 read from the same actor for higher-confidence prioritization — an actor reading a password and then delaying its rotation is a strong credential-persistence signal.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification (rare — typically only during specific maintenance-window extensions).
Check for a recent password read from the same actor.
response_guidance: Revert the expiration time and force an immediate password rotation.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: LAPS Password History Attribute Read (Windows LAPS)
description: Detects a read of the Windows LAPS password-history attribute (msLAPS-PasswordHistory), which retains previously rotated passwords for recovery scenarios. Access to password history extends an attacker's window of useful stolen credentials backward in time and may reveal a password pattern if rotation policy is weak.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 4662 with Properties containing msLAPS-PasswordHistory.

detection_logic: Event ID 4662 where Properties includes msLAPS-PasswordHistory, and Subject_Account_Name is not in authorized_laps_readers.csv.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4662
| search Properties="*msLAPS-PasswordHistory*"
| lookup authorized_laps_readers.csv Subject_Account_Name OUTPUT is_authorized
| where isnull(is_authorized)
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_Name
tuning_guidance: Requires DS Access auditing on the password-history attribute specifically; only applicable to Windows LAPS (Windows Server 2023+/modern LAPS), not legacy LAPS.
investigation_steps: Same as AD-LAPS-001, extended to any historical password the target computer has used.
response_guidance: Rotate the target computer's current password and treat any retained history as compromised.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: LAPS Password Read Immediately Followed by Local Administrator Authentication (Chain)
description: The flagship LAPS-to-lateral-movement chain: an actor reads a computer's LAPS password (AD-LAPS-001) and shortly afterward a local Administrator/local-admin-equivalent authentication occurs against that same computer from a source other than the computer itself. This sequence is a near-complete confirmation that the read credential was actually used, converting a credential-access finding into an active lateral-movement event.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log (LAPS read) correlated with the target computer's own security event log (4624 local Administrator logon) within a short window.

detection_logic: AD-LAPS-001 match where the target computer (Object_Name) subsequently shows an Event ID 4624 local Administrator logon within 24 hours from a source other than the computer's own baseline management source.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4662
| search Properties="*ms-Mcs-AdmPwd*" OR Properties="*msLAPS-Password*"
| eval etype="laps_read"
| append [
    search index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4624 Account_Name="Administrator"
    | eval etype="local_admin_logon"
    | rename dvc as Object_Name
  ]
| transaction Object_Name maxspan=24h startswith=eval(etype="laps_read") endswith=eval(etype="local_admin_logon")
| where eventcount=2
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_Name, duration
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches from unauthorized readers (per AD-LAPS-001's authorization check); for authorized readers this sequence is expected routine behavior and should be excluded.
investigation_steps: Confirm the authenticating source and whether it matches the reading account's own context.
Review what actions were performed during the local-admin session.
response_guidance: Treat as an active, confirmed lateral-movement event; rotate the password again, terminate the session, and investigate the reading account's initial compromise vector.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: gMSA Managed Password Read Immediately Followed by Authentication as the gMSA from a New Host (Chain)
description: Detects a gMSA managed-password read followed shortly afterward by the gMSA authenticating from a source host not previously seen in its baseline. Since gMSAs are designed to only be usable from hosts explicitly permitted to retrieve the password, authentication from a new source immediately after an unauthorized read is a strong confirmation that the credential was actively used for lateral movement or service impersonation.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 4662 (managed-password read) followed by 4768/4624 for the gMSA identity from a new source within a short window.

detection_logic: AD-LAPS-004 match followed within 4 hours by an Event ID 4768/4624 for the same gMSA account from a source not in service_account_src_baseline.csv.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4662
| search Properties="*msDS-ManagedPassword*"
| eval etype="gmsa_read"
| append [
    search index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" (EventCode=4768 OR EventCode=4624)
    | lookup service_account_src_baseline.csv Account_Name, Source_Network_Address OUTPUT is_baseline
    | where isnull(is_baseline)
    | eval etype="gmsa_new_source_auth"
    | rename Account_Name as Object_Name
  ]
| transaction Object_Name maxspan=4h startswith=eval(etype="gmsa_read") endswith=eval(etype="gmsa_new_source_auth")
| where eventcount=2
| table _time, dvc, Object_Name, duration
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches; requires service_account_src_baseline.csv to be reasonably comprehensive to avoid false positives during legitimate new-host onboarding.
investigation_steps: Identify the new source host and account performing the read.
Review what the gMSA authenticated to and any actions taken.
response_guidance: Treat as an active, likely successful service-account-impersonation attack; investigate the reading account's access path and review the gMSA's retrieval delegation.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: New Security Support Provider Registered on a Domain Controller
description: Detects a new entry added to the Security Packages (Security Support Provider) registry value on a domain controller. Registering a malicious SSP is the boot-persistent form of the LSASS in-memory patching technique flagged in AD-DC-021 — the malicious DLL loads automatically at every LSASS start (including after reboot) and can implement credential interception or authentication-bypass behavior.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 4657 on HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\Security Packages.

detection_logic: Event ID 4657 on the Security Packages registry value where the new value contains an entry not in expected_lsass_modules.csv.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4657 Object_Name="*Control\\Lsa\\Security Packages"
| lookup domain_controllers.csv computer_name AS dvc OUTPUT is_dc
| where is_dc=1
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_Name, New_Value
tuning_guidance: Requires registry SACL auditing on this key. Alert on all matches without exception.
investigation_steps: Identify the new package name and locate the corresponding DLL on disk.
Assume the technique is active and check for authentication anomalies domain-wide.
Treat with equal severity to AD-DC-021.
response_guidance: Remove the registry entry and the malicious DLL, reboot the DC to clear it from LSASS, and force a domain-wide credential reset.

references.title: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Security Support Provider

author: Threat Detection Library

title: New Authentication or Notification Package Registered
description: Detects a new entry added to the Authentication Packages or Notification Packages registry values on a domain controller. A malicious Notification Package DLL is loaded by lsass.exe and receives password-change events in cleartext before hashing — the classic 'password filter' credential-theft persistence technique, capturing every password set or changed domain-wide from that point forward.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 4657 on HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\Authentication Packages or \Notification Packages.

detection_logic: Event ID 4657 on the Authentication Packages or Notification Packages registry value on a domain controller where the new value contains an entry not in expected_lsass_modules.csv.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4657 (Object_Name="*Control\\Lsa\\Authentication Packages" OR Object_Name="*Control\\Lsa\\Notification Packages")
| lookup domain_controllers.csv computer_name AS dvc OUTPUT is_dc
| where is_dc=1
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_Name, New_Value
tuning_guidance: Requires registry SACL auditing. Alert on all matches without exception; this is one of the most severe persistence techniques in the catalogue since it captures every future password change in cleartext, not just currently-cached credentials.
investigation_steps: Identify the new package name and locate/analyze the corresponding DLL.
Assume every password changed since the DLL was registered has been captured by the attacker.
Force a domain-wide password reset for every account that changed its password during the exposure window.
response_guidance: Remove the registry entry and the malicious DLL, reboot the DC, and force a domain-wide password reset covering the entire exposure window — this is functionally equivalent to a full credential-database compromise for any account whose password changed while the filter was active.

references.title: Modify Authentication Process: Password Filter DLL

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Permanent WMI Event Subscription Created on a Domain Controller
description: Detects a permanent WMI event subscription (EventFilter, EventConsumer, and FilterToConsumerBinding) being created on a domain controller. WMI subscriptions are a well-documented fileless persistence mechanism that triggers execution in response to a system event (e.g. a scheduled interval, logon, or process start) and survives reboots without needing a registered service or scheduled task.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-WMI-Activity/Operational
data_sources.description: WMI-Activity Operational log, Event ID 5861 (permanent event consumer registered) or Sysmon Event ID 19/20/21 (WMI event filter/consumer/binding activity).

detection_logic: Sysmon Event ID 19/20/21, or WMI-Activity Operational log Event ID 5861, on a domain controller.
spl:
(index=sysmon sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" (EventCode=19 OR EventCode=20 OR EventCode=21)) OR (index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-WMI-Activity/Operational" EventCode=5861)
| lookup domain_controllers.csv computer_name AS dvc OUTPUT is_dc
| where is_dc=1
| table _time, dvc, EventCode
tuning_guidance: Requires Sysmon WMI-event logging or the WMI-Activity Operational log enabled on domain controllers — an explicit telemetry dependency. Alert on all matches; permanent WMI subscriptions on a DC should be exceptionally rare.
investigation_steps: Retrieve the filter query, consumer type, and binding to understand the trigger condition and payload.
Assume the payload has already executed if the trigger condition has occurred since creation.
response_guidance: Remove the WMI subscription (filter, consumer, and binding) and investigate the creating account and process for the initial access vector.

references.title: Event Triggered Execution: Windows Management Instrumentation Event Subscription

author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires Sysmon WMI-event logging (Event IDs 19-21) or the WMI-Activity Operational log enabled on domain controllers; not captured by default Windows Security auditing.

title: Shadow Credentials: msDS-KeyCredentialLink Added to a Privileged Account
description: Detects an attacker-controlled public key being added to a Tier-0 object's msDS-KeyCredentialLink attribute (the 'Shadow Credentials' technique, implemented by tools like Whisker/Certipy). This modern technique lets the attacker authenticate as the target account using Windows Hello for Business/PKINIT certificate-based logon derived from their own key pair — without ever needing or changing the account's actual password — making it a particularly stealthy persistence mechanism that bypasses password-based credential-rotation remediation entirely.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on msDS-KeyCredentialLink for a Tier-0 or privileged-service-account object.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name=msDS-KeyCredentialLink, and Object_DN is in tier0_privileged_accounts.csv, from an actor not in authorized_identity_admins.csv.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="msDS-KeyCredentialLink"
| lookup tier0_privileged_accounts.csv object_dn AS Object_DN OUTPUT is_privileged
| where is_privileged=1
| lookup authorized_identity_admins.csv Subject_Account_Name OUTPUT is_expected
| where isnull(is_expected)
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches for Tier-0 objects; this attribute change is rare enough outside a documented Windows Hello for Business rollout to warrant per-occurrence review even for non-Tier-0 accounts.
investigation_steps: Determine whether this reflects a legitimate Windows Hello for Business enrollment for the account.
If not, treat as an active persistence attempt and check for subsequent PKINIT-based (certificate) authentication as this account.
response_guidance: Remove the unauthorized key credential immediately; note that removing it does not require a password reset (unlike most other credential-theft remediations) but should still be paired with a review of the account's overall exposure.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Certificate Template Modified to Enable Client Authentication Without Approval
description: Detects a certificate template's configuration being changed to enable a client-authentication-capable EKU (Client Authentication, Smart Card Logon, or the 'Any Purpose'/no-EKU wildcard) while manager approval remains disabled and enrollee-supplied subject names are permitted — the classic ESC1 misconfiguration that lets any enrollment-permitted principal request a certificate for an arbitrary UPN, including a Domain Admin's, and authenticate as that user without any approval step.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on certificate-template attributes (pKIExtendedKeyUsage, msPKI-Enrollment-Flag, msPKI-Certificate-Name-Flag) under the Certificate Templates container.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 under CN=Certificate Templates,CN=Public Key Services,CN=Services,CN=Configuration where the attribute changed is pKIExtendedKeyUsage, msPKI-Enrollment-Flag, or msPKI-Certificate-Name-Flag.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136
| where match(Object_DN, "CN=Certificate Templates,CN=Public Key Services,CN=Services,CN=Configuration")
| where Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name IN ("pKIExtendedKeyUsage","msPKI-Enrollment-Flag","msPKI-Certificate-Name-Flag")
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name, Attribute_Value
tuning_guidance: Flag matches for manual review to determine whether the resulting combination constitutes an ESC1-class misconfiguration (client-auth EKU + no manager approval + enrollee-supplied subject); this SPL surfaces candidate changes rather than definitively classifying the resulting risk, since that requires evaluating the template's full combined configuration, not a single attribute in isolation.
investigation_steps: Retrieve the template's full current configuration and evaluate it against known ESC1-ESC8 misconfiguration patterns.
Identify who has enrollment rights on the affected template (correlate AD-ACL-018).
Check the CA's issued-certificate log for any certificates already issued from the modified template.
response_guidance: Revert the template configuration or restrict enrollment rights immediately if a dangerous combination is confirmed; revoke any certificates already issued under the vulnerable configuration.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Determining whether a change constitutes an exploitable ESC1-class misconfiguration requires evaluating the template's complete combined configuration (EKU + enrollment flags + name flags + enrollment ACL), not any single attribute change in isolation; this detection surfaces candidate changes for that manual/tooled evaluation rather than a definitive verdict.

title: New Certificate Template Published to a Certificate Authority
description: Detects a certificate template being newly published (made available for enrollment) on an Enterprise Certificate Authority. Each newly published template is a new potential attack surface; if the template itself carries a dangerous configuration (see AD-PERSIST-005) or is later modified to one, publishing it is the step that makes it actually reachable by enrollers.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on certificateTemplates attribute of a pKIEnrollmentService object (the CA's published-template list).

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name=certificateTemplates on a pKIEnrollmentService object.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="certificateTemplates"
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, Attribute_Value
tuning_guidance: Maintain pki_management_principals.csv for expected publishers; escalate if the actor is unexpected or the template being published is itself flagged risky.
investigation_steps: Review the newly published template's configuration.
Confirm business justification.
response_guidance: Unpublish if unauthorized or misconfigured.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Certificate Authority Management Rights (Manage CA / Manage Certificates) Granted to Unexpected Principal
description: Detects the Manage CA or Manage Certificates security right on an Enterprise Certificate Authority being granted to a principal outside the expected PKI-administration group. Manage CA rights allow full administrative control of the CA (including approving pending requests and modifying CA-level configuration such as which templates are trusted), while Manage Certificates allows issuing/denying/revoking certificates — either is a high-value persistence and privilege-escalation target since the CA is the root of trust for all certificate-based authentication in the environment.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: CA server security event log, Event ID 4899/4900 (certificate services security settings changed) or DC 5136 on the CA object's nTSecurityDescriptor.

detection_logic: Event ID 4899/4900 on the CA server, or Event ID 5136 on a pKIEnrollmentService object's nTSecurityDescriptor, where the grantee is not in pki_management_principals.csv.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" (EventCode=4899 OR EventCode=4900)
| lookup pki_management_principals.csv Subject_Account_Name OUTPUT is_expected
| where isnull(is_expected)
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name
tuning_guidance: Requires CA auditing enabled (Certification Authority MMC > Properties > Auditing) in addition to standard DC auditing — a distinct telemetry source from the domain-controller-centric logging most of this catalogue relies on. Alert on all matches.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for the elevated CA rights.
Review the CA's recent issued/denied certificate activity for signs of abuse.
response_guidance: Remove unauthorized CA administrative rights immediately; treat as an active attempt to gain control of the PKI trust root.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires Certification Authority role-specific auditing to be explicitly enabled on the CA server, a separate configuration step from standard domain-controller security auditing.

title: Unauthorized Certificate Added to the NTAuth Store
description: Detects a certificate being added to the NTAuthCertificates object in the Configuration partition. Only CA certificates present in NTAuth are trusted by domain controllers to issue certificates usable for AD authentication (PKINIT); an attacker who adds their own rogue CA certificate here can then issue self-signed certificates for any identity that domain controllers will accept for logon — a powerful, durable persistence mechanism independent of any single account's credentials.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on cACertificate attribute of the NTAuthCertificates object.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where Object_DN matches 'CN=NTAuthCertificates,CN=Public Key Services,CN=Services,CN=Configuration' and Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name=cACertificate.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="cACertificate"
| where match(Object_DN, "CN=NTAuthCertificates,CN=Public Key Services,CN=Services,CN=Configuration")
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, Attribute_Value
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches without exception; this should be an exceptionally rare, deliberate change tied only to legitimate new CA deployment or renewal.
investigation_steps: Identify the added certificate's issuer, subject, and validity period.
Confirm it corresponds to a known, legitimate CA in the environment.
If not recognized, assume a rogue trust-anchor has been established for certificate-based authentication forgery.
response_guidance: Remove the unrecognized certificate immediately and treat as a severe, durable persistence compromise; review all certificate-based authentication events since the addition for signs of abuse.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Certificate Issued for a Privileged UPN Requested by a Non-Privileged Principal
description: Detects the CA issuing a certificate whose subject alternative name (SAN) UPN corresponds to a Tier-0/privileged account, where the requesting principal is a different, non-privileged identity. This is the exploitation step of an ESC1-class attack: a low-privileged enrollee requests a certificate on a vulnerable template while supplying a privileged user's UPN in the request, and the CA issues it without verifying the requester actually owns that identity.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: CA server security event log, Event ID 4886/4887 (certificate request/issuance) with the requester identity and the issued certificate's SAN UPN.

detection_logic: CA Event ID 4887 (certificate issued) where the SAN UPN corresponds to an account in tier0_privileged_accounts.csv and Requester is a different account not in authorized_identity_admins.csv.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4887
| lookup tier0_privileged_accounts.csv account AS SAN_UPN OUTPUT is_privileged_upn
| where is_privileged_upn=1
| where Requester!=SAN_UPN
| lookup authorized_identity_admins.csv Requester OUTPUT is_expected_requester
| where isnull(is_expected_requester)
| table _time, dvc, Requester, SAN_UPN
tuning_guidance: Requires CA-specific auditing enabled and a log source that surfaces both the requester identity and the certificate's SAN UPN separately — validate field availability against the deployed CA logging configuration. Alert on all matches without exception.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed ESC1-class exploitation.
Revoke the issued certificate immediately.
Identify and remediate the vulnerable template (correlate AD-PERSIST-005).
Assume the privileged account's identity has been fully compromised via certificate-based authentication.
response_guidance: Revoke the certificate, publish the revocation to CRL/OCSP, remediate the vulnerable template, and treat as a full compromise of the impersonated privileged account — reset its credentials and review all activity performed under its identity since issuance.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires Certification Authority role-specific auditing with both requester identity and issued-certificate SAN UPN available as separate, correlatable fields; validate this against the actual CA logging configuration before deployment.

title: Schema Default Security Descriptor Modified for a Sensitive Object Class
description: Detects the defaultSecurityDescriptor attribute being modified on a schema class definition (e.g. the user or group class). Because this attribute determines the default ACL applied to every future object of that class created domain-wide, an attacker who weakens it establishes a persistence mechanism that automatically grants them elevated rights over every new object created afterward — a technique that can remain effective long after the specific accounts/objects involved in the original compromise are cleaned up, since it silently poisons all future object creation.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on defaultSecurityDescriptor under the Schema naming context.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name=defaultSecurityDescriptor.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="defaultSecurityDescriptor"
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, Attribute_Value
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches without exception; this is one of the most severe and durable persistence techniques covered in this catalogue and should be exceptionally rare outside a very deliberate, expert-reviewed schema project.
investigation_steps: Identify exactly which class's default ACL changed and how.
Assess every object of that class created since the change for the newly inherited (potentially attacker-favorable) permissions.
Engage AD-schema expertise before attempting remediation.
response_guidance: Revert the defaultSecurityDescriptor to its original value and manually review/correct the ACL on every object of that class created since the change — schema-default poisoning does not self-heal via SDProp the way AdminSDHolder does.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Registry Run Key Pushed to Multiple Computers via GPO Preferences
description: Detects a GPO Preferences registry item targeting a Run/RunOnce autostart key being added to a GPO. Like scheduled tasks (AD-GPO-007), this is a fleet-wide persistence mechanism, but delivered via the Registry.xml GPP extension instead of ScheduledTasks.xml, executing the configured command for every user or on every computer the GPO applies to at next logon/startup.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: File-system auditing Event ID 4663 on a GPO's Preferences\Registry\Registry.xml file.

detection_logic: Event ID 4663 write access on '*\Preferences\Registry\Registry.xml' under a GPO's SYSVOL folder.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4663 Object_Name="*\\Preferences\\Registry\\Registry.xml"
| search Accesses="*WriteData*" OR Accesses="*AppendData*"
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_Name
tuning_guidance: Requires SYSVOL SACL auditing. Correlate with the GPO's link scope for prioritization, following the same pattern as AD-GPO-007.
investigation_steps: Retrieve and review the Registry.xml content for the specific Run-key command being pushed.
Identify the GPO's link scope and check target endpoints for the resulting persistence entry.
response_guidance: Remove the malicious registry item from the GPO and hunt across affected endpoints for evidence of the pushed persistence.

references.title: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Logon Script Attribute (scriptPath) Set on a Privileged User Object
description: Detects the scriptPath attribute being set or changed on a Tier-0/privileged user object. Unlike a GPO-delivered logon script (AD-GPO-019), scriptPath is an attribute of the individual user object itself and executes whenever that specific user logs on interactively — a narrowly targeted persistence mechanism that runs specifically in the context of the privileged user, independent of which computer they log on to.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on scriptPath attribute of a user object flagged as Tier-0/privileged.

detection_logic: Event ID 5136 where Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name=scriptPath and Object_DN is in tier0_privileged_accounts.csv.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136 Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="scriptPath"
| lookup tier0_privileged_accounts.csv object_dn AS Object_DN OUTPUT is_privileged
| where is_privileged=1
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_DN, Attribute_Value
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches for privileged accounts; scriptPath is a legacy attribute rarely used in modern environments outside specific legacy application requirements.
investigation_steps: Retrieve the referenced script and review its content.
Confirm business justification.
Check for the script's next execution at the account's subsequent logon.
response_guidance: Clear the attribute if unauthorized and investigate the modifying actor.

references.title: Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts: Logon Script (Windows)

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Multiple Distinct Persistence Mechanisms Established by the Same Actor (Chain)
description: The flagship persistence chain: the same actor establishes two or more distinct persistence mechanisms from this namespace and related ACL/GPO/delegation namespaces within a short window — for example, an ACL grant on a Tier-0 object followed by a Shadow Credentials addition, or a GPO change followed by an AdminSDHolder modification. Attackers who successfully compromise Tier-0 typically plant multiple redundant persistence mechanisms specifically so that remediating any single one does not fully evict them; detecting the pattern of multiple distinct mechanisms from one actor is a higher-confidence signal of a thorough, deliberate compromise than any single mechanism alone.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, correlating distinct persistence-indicator event types (ACL grants, GPO changes, delegation changes, Shadow Credentials, SSP/AP registration) by actor.

detection_logic: Two or more distinct persistence-category matches (AD-ACL-001/002/003/007/010/019, AD-GPO-002/010, AD-DELEG-003/006, AD-PERSIST-001/002/004/008/010) from the same Subject_Account_Name within 24 hours.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5136
| eval persist_category=case(
    Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="nTSecurityDescriptor", "acl_grant",
    Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo" OR Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity", "delegation_grant",
    Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="msDS-KeyCredentialLink", "shadow_credentials",
    Attribute_LDAP_Display_Name="cACertificate", "ntauth_cert",
    true(), null()
  )
| where isnotnull(persist_category)
| bucket _time span=24h
| stats dc(persist_category) as distinct_mechanisms values(persist_category) as mechanisms by _time, Subject_Account_Name
| where distinct_mechanisms >= 2
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches without exception; while each individual underlying event is already independently high-severity, this correlation elevates confidence and urgency for incident-response scoping purposes.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed, thorough Tier-0 compromise with multiple redundant persistence mechanisms.
Enumerate and remediate every mechanism found, not just the first one identified.
Engage full incident response with the assumption that remediation of a single finding will not fully evict the attacker.
response_guidance: Full domain-compromise incident response: krbtgt double-reset, comprehensive persistence-mechanism sweep across every namespace in this catalogue, and credential rotation for all privileged accounts.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Certificate Enrollment Agent Rights Granted to an Unexpected Principal
description: Detects a principal being granted Certificate Request Agent (Enrollment Agent) rights via a certificate template. An account holding an enrollment-agent certificate can request certificates on behalf of other users (subject to template restrictions) — a legitimate feature for smart-card issuance workflows that, if granted broadly, becomes an ESC3-class certificate-based impersonation path similar in effect to constrained delegation.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 5136 on a certificate template's nTSecurityDescriptor granting Enrollment Agent-related rights, or issuance of an Enrollment Agent certificate itself (CA Event ID 4887).

detection_logic: Event ID 4887 (certificate issued) where the issued certificate's template corresponds to the built-in Enrollment Agent template or a custom template with the Certificate Request Agent EKU, issued to a principal not in pki_management_principals.csv.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4887
| lookup enrollment_agent_templates.csv CertificateTemplate OUTPUT is_enrollment_agent_template
| where is_enrollment_agent_template=1
| lookup pki_management_principals.csv Requester OUTPUT is_expected
| where isnull(is_expected)
| table _time, dvc, Requester, CertificateTemplate
tuning_guidance: Requires CA-specific auditing enabled and a maintained enrollment_agent_templates.csv identifying which templates carry the Certificate Request Agent EKU.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification for enrollment-agent rights.
Review what certificates the agent has subsequently requested on behalf of other users.
response_guidance: Revoke the enrollment-agent certificate if unauthorized and restrict the template's issuance policy.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires Certification Authority role-specific auditing to be explicitly enabled, plus a maintained inventory of which templates carry the Certificate Request Agent EKU.

title: Break-Glass/Emergency Account Used Outside a Declared Emergency
description: Detects authentication using a designated break-glass/emergency-access account outside a formally declared emergency-access event. Break-glass accounts are intentionally excluded from routine MFA/PAM controls to guarantee access during a genuine crisis, making them an attractive, durable persistence target if an attacker discovers and quietly begins using one without triggering the emergency-declaration process that would normally draw scrutiny to its use.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 4624/4768 for an account in breakglass_accounts.csv, correlated against a declared-emergency lookup.

detection_logic: Event ID 4624/4768 where Account_Name is in breakglass_accounts.csv and no matching entry exists in declared_emergency_events.csv for the timestamp.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" (EventCode=4624 OR EventCode=4768)
| lookup breakglass_accounts.csv account AS Account_Name OUTPUT is_breakglass
| where is_breakglass=1
| lookup declared_emergency_events.csv account AS Account_Name OUTPUT window_start, window_end
| where isnull(window_start) OR _time < window_start OR _time > window_end
| table _time, dvc, Account_Name
tuning_guidance: Requires maintaining both breakglass_accounts.csv and a process for logging declared_emergency_events.csv whenever break-glass access is legitimately invoked. Alert on all matches without exception.
investigation_steps: Immediately contact the account owner/custodian to confirm whether this is a legitimate, undeclared emergency use versus unauthorized access.
Review the account's session activity.
response_guidance: If unauthorized, treat as an active Tier-0 compromise using a control-bypass account; reset the account's credentials immediately and review its recent activity in full.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: SAM, SECURITY, or SYSTEM Registry Hive Saved to Disk
description: Detects the reg.exe save command (or an equivalent API call) being used to export the SAM, SECURITY, or SYSTEM registry hive to a file. This is the classic offline local-credential-dumping technique: the exported hives contain the local SAM database and the LSA secrets/boot key needed to decrypt cached domain credentials, enabling extraction without touching lsass.exe memory directly.

data_sources.name: Sysmon Event ID 1
data_sources.description: Process creation for reg.exe with save arguments targeting HKLM\SAM, HKLM\SECURITY, or HKLM\SYSTEM.

detection_logic: Sysmon Event ID 1 where Image ends in reg.exe and CommandLine matches 'save' combined with 'HKLM\SAM', 'HKLM\SECURITY', or 'HKLM\SYSTEM'.
spl:
index=sysmon sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1
| where match(Image, "(?i)reg\.exe$") AND match(CommandLine, "(?i)save") AND match(CommandLine, "(?i)HKLM\\(SAM|SECURITY|SYSTEM)")
| table _time, dvc, User, Image, CommandLine
tuning_guidance: Requires Sysmon (or equivalent EDR process-creation telemetry) — an explicit dependency beyond native Windows Security auditing. Exclude known backup-solution service accounts performing legitimate system-state backups.
investigation_steps: Identify the exported file's destination and check whether it was subsequently copied off the host.
Assume local credential and cached domain-credential exposure for the affected host.
Check for the same actor/host performing this against multiple hosts (lateral SAM dumping).
response_guidance: Delete the exported hive files, reset local Administrator and any exposed cached-credential passwords, and investigate the actor's broader activity.

references.title: OS Credential Dumping: Security Account Manager

author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires Sysmon or equivalent EDR process-creation/command-line telemetry; not observable from default Windows Security event logging.

title: WDigest UseLogonCredential Registry Value Enabled
description: Detects the WDigest UseLogonCredential registry value being set to 1, which forces LSASS to retain a reversibly-encrypted (effectively cleartext-recoverable) copy of the logged-on user's password in memory for the WDigest authentication provider. This is a well-known technique to make LSASS memory dumps (e.g. via Mimikatz sekurlsa::wdigest) yield cleartext passwords rather than only hashes, on hosts where this was patched to default-off.
required_log_sources: Windows Security Event Log (all domain-joined hosts)

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: Security event log, Event ID 4657 on HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest\UseLogonCredential.

detection_logic: Event ID 4657 on the UseLogonCredential registry value where New_Value=1.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4657 Object_Name="*WDigest\\UseLogonCredential"
| where New_Value="1"
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_Name, New_Value
tuning_guidance: Requires registry SACL auditing on this key. Alert on all matches without exception; this value should remain at its secure default (0/absent) on virtually all modern hosts.
investigation_steps: Confirm no legitimate reason (there essentially isn't one in a modern environment) exists for this change.
Check for a subsequent LSASS memory dump on the same host.
Assume any subsequent interactive logon's password is recoverable in cleartext while this setting remains active.
response_guidance: Revert the value to 0 immediately and treat any account that logged on interactively while it was enabled as having a potentially exposed cleartext password.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: LSA Protection (RunAsPPL) Disabled
description: Detects the LSA Protection (RunAsPPL) registry value being disabled. When enabled, LSA Protection runs lsass.exe as a Protected Process Light, blocking even administrator-level processes from opening a memory-read handle to it without a signed, Microsoft-approved driver. Disabling this control directly reopens the standard LSASS-memory-dumping attack surface on the affected host.
required_log_sources: Windows Security Event Log (all domain-joined hosts)

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: Security event log, Event ID 4657 on HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\RunAsPPL.

detection_logic: Event ID 4657 on the RunAsPPL registry value where New_Value=0 and Old_Value was non-zero.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4657 Object_Name="*Control\\Lsa\\RunAsPPL"
| where New_Value="0" AND Old_Value!="0"
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_Name, Old_Value, New_Value
tuning_guidance: Requires registry SACL auditing. Alert on all matches for Tier-0/privileged-user-accessed hosts; treat as high priority everywhere else as well since this specifically defeats a key credential-theft mitigation.
investigation_steps: Confirm business justification (rare — typically only certain legacy driver-compatibility scenarios).
Check for a subsequent LSASS access attempt (correlate AD-DC-008 pattern applied to this host) now that the protection is removed.
response_guidance: Re-enable LSA Protection immediately (requires a reboot to take effect) and treat the exposure window as elevated LSASS-dumping risk.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: LSASS Memory Dump Created via comsvcs.dll MiniDump or Task Manager
description: Detects the specific process/command-line pattern for dumping lsass.exe memory via rundll32.exe invoking comsvcs.dll's MiniDump export, or via Task Manager's 'Create dump file' feature, on any domain-joined host (a broader, non-DC-specific companion to AD-DC-008). Both are living-off-the-land techniques that avoid dropping a separate credential-dumping binary on disk.

data_sources.name: Sysmon Event ID 1
data_sources.description: Process creation for rundll32.exe with comsvcs.dll MiniDump arguments targeting an lsass.exe PID.

detection_logic: Sysmon Event ID 1 where Image ends in rundll32.exe and CommandLine contains 'comsvcs.dll' and 'MiniDump'.
spl:
index=sysmon sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1
| where match(Image, "(?i)rundll32\.exe$") AND match(CommandLine, "(?i)comsvcs\.dll") AND match(CommandLine, "(?i)minidump")
| table _time, dvc, User, Image, CommandLine
tuning_guidance: Requires Sysmon or equivalent EDR process-creation telemetry. Alert on all matches without exception.
investigation_steps: Identify the dump file's destination and check for exfiltration.
Assume every credential cached in that host's LSASS memory is compromised.
Check for privileged-account logons to the affected host prior to the dump.
response_guidance: Delete the dump file, reset credentials for every account that had a cached session on the host, and investigate the actor's initial access.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires Sysmon or equivalent EDR process-creation/command-line telemetry; not observable from default Windows Security event logging.

title: Known Credential-Dumping Tool Command-Line Pattern Observed
description: Detects command-line arguments matching well-known credential-dumping tooling syntax — Mimikatz module invocations (sekurlsa::, lsadump::, kerberos::, crypto::), Rubeus command verbs (asktgt, s4u, kerberoast, dump), or similar signature strings — regardless of the executable's filename, since attackers frequently rename these binaries to evade filename-based detection.

data_sources.name: Sysmon Event ID 1
data_sources.description: Process creation where CommandLine matches known credential-dumping tool syntax patterns.

detection_logic: Sysmon Event ID 1 where CommandLine matches any of: 'sekurlsa::', 'lsadump::', 'kerberos::', 'privilege::debug', 'asktgt', 's4u', 'kerberoast', 'dcsync', 'ptt' (pass-the-ticket).
spl:
index=sysmon sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1
| where match(CommandLine, "(?i)(sekurlsa::|lsadump::|kerberos::purge|privilege::debug|asktgt|s4u|/kerberoast|dcsync|ptt\s)")
| table _time, dvc, User, Image, CommandLine
tuning_guidance: Requires Sysmon or equivalent EDR command-line telemetry. This pattern-matching approach catches renamed binaries but will miss attackers who avoid these specific documented syntax strings (e.g. custom in-house tooling, obfuscated command lines, or reflective in-memory loading that bypasses command-line logging entirely) — treat as one detection layer among several, not a complete credential-dumping control.
investigation_steps: Review the full process tree and parent process for the flagged command.
Assume the underlying credential-access action succeeded and follow the response guidance for whichever specific technique the syntax indicates (DCSync, Kerberoasting, Pass-the-Ticket, etc.).
response_guidance: Treat as an active, high-confidence credential-dumping tool execution; isolate the host and follow the response procedure for the specific technique indicated by the matched syntax.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires Sysmon or equivalent EDR command-line telemetry; this signature-based approach will not catch attackers who avoid these specific documented syntax strings, use custom tooling, or load reflectively in memory to bypass command-line logging.

title: DPAPI Master Key File Accessed by an Unexpected Process
description: Detects a process other than the expected Windows DPAPI subsystem accessing a user's DPAPI master key file (under %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Protect\<SID>). DPAPI master keys, once obtained (and decrypted using either the user's password or the domain backup key held by domain controllers), can be used to decrypt saved credentials, browser passwords, Wi-Fi keys, and other DPAPI-protected secrets on the host.

data_sources.name: Sysmon Event ID 11
data_sources.description: File create/access events for paths under '\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Protect\' by a process other than lsass.exe or the owning user's expected session.

detection_logic: Sysmon Event ID 11 where TargetFilename matches '*\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Protect\*' and Image is not a recognized system process.
spl:
index=sysmon sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=11
| where match(TargetFilename, "(?i)\\AppData\\Roaming\\Microsoft\\Protect\\")
| where NOT match(Image, "(?i)(lsass|dpapisrv|svchost)\.exe$")
| table _time, dvc, User, Image, TargetFilename
tuning_guidance: Requires Sysmon file-monitoring telemetry, which can be verbose if not scoped; restrict collection to the Protect folder path specifically.
investigation_steps: Identify the accessing process and its purpose.
Check for a subsequent domain-backup-key request (DPAPI domain backup key retrieval, a DC-based operation) or offline DPAPI-decryption tooling.
response_guidance: Investigate as potential credential-vault theft; if confirmed, reset any credentials that may have been stored via DPAPI-protected applications on the host.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires Sysmon or equivalent EDR file-access telemetry; not observable from default Windows Security event logging.

title: DPAPI Domain Backup Key Retrieved from a Domain Controller
description: Detects a request for the domain's DPAPI backup key (BACKUPKEY_RETRIEVE), which domain controllers hold specifically to allow master-key recovery when a user's own password is unavailable. An attacker who obtains this domain-wide backup key can decrypt any DPAPI-protected secret for any user in the domain, regardless of that user's own password — making its theft roughly equivalent in impact to a DCSync of the domain's credential material, but for DPAPI-protected data specifically.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 4662 with Properties referencing the BackupKey RPC interface/control-access right, from a non-DC or non-recognized-DPAPI-recovery-tooling source.

detection_logic: Event ID 4662 reflecting a BackupKey retrieval operation from a source not in dcsync_authorized_principals.csv or a documented DPAPI-recovery-tooling allowlist.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4662
| search Properties="*BackupKey*"
| lookup dcsync_authorized_principals.csv trustee AS Subject_Account_Name OUTPUT is_authorized
| where isnull(is_authorized)
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, IpAddress
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches without exception; this is one of the highest-impact single events possible for DPAPI-protected credential exposure domain-wide.
investigation_steps: Treat as a full domain-wide DPAPI-decryption capability having been obtained by the requesting principal.
Identify the source and its authorization.
response_guidance: Treat with equal urgency to a DCSync attack; investigate immediately and consider the domain's DPAPI backup key compromised, planning for eventual key rollover per Microsoft guidance.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Credential Manager Vault Enumerated or Exported via Command Line
description: Detects command-line usage of vaultcmd.exe, cmdkey.exe /list, or PowerShell credential-manager enumeration cmdlets. Windows Credential Manager stores saved network credentials (including RDP-saved credentials and mapped-drive passwords) that an attacker can enumerate and, in some cases, extract for reuse.

data_sources.name: Sysmon Event ID 1
data_sources.description: Process creation for vaultcmd.exe or cmdkey.exe with list/enumeration arguments.

detection_logic: Sysmon Event ID 1 where Image matches vaultcmd.exe/cmdkey.exe and CommandLine includes list/enumeration syntax.
spl:
index=sysmon sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1
| where match(Image, "(?i)(vaultcmd|cmdkey)\.exe$") AND match(CommandLine, "(?i)(/list|/listcreds)")
| table _time, dvc, User, Image, CommandLine
tuning_guidance: Requires Sysmon or equivalent EDR command-line telemetry. This is a routine, low-privilege reconnaissance action with legitimate administrative uses — treat as a lower-priority supporting signal rather than a standalone high-severity alert.
investigation_steps: Identify the source account and host.
Check for subsequent use of any enumerated credentials elsewhere in the environment.
response_guidance: Investigate if unexplained; not independently high-urgency.

references.title: Credentials from Password Stores: Windows Credential Manager

author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires Sysmon or equivalent EDR command-line telemetry; not observable from default Windows Security event logging.

title: Kerberos Ticket Cache Exported to a .kirbi File
description: Detects a file being written with a .kirbi extension, or Sysmon command-line evidence of a ticket-export operation (Mimikatz kerberos::list /export, Rubeus dump). A .kirbi file is a serialized Kerberos ticket that can be reimported and reused (Pass-the-Ticket) from a different host, so its creation on disk is a strong signal that ticket material is being staged for exfiltration or lateral reuse.

data_sources.name: Sysmon Event ID 11
data_sources.description: File create events for a filename ending in .kirbi.

detection_logic: Sysmon Event ID 11 where TargetFilename ends in '.kirbi'.
spl:
index=sysmon sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=11
| where match(TargetFilename, "(?i)\.kirbi$")
| table _time, dvc, Image, TargetFilename
tuning_guidance: Requires Sysmon file-monitoring telemetry. Alert on all matches without exception; the .kirbi extension has no common legitimate use outside deliberate Kerberos-ticket-handling tooling.
investigation_steps: Identify the exported ticket's associated account (via the creating process's context).
Check for exfiltration of the file or reuse (import) on a different host.
Assume the associated account's Kerberos session is compromised for the ticket's remaining validity period.
response_guidance: Delete the exported ticket file, reset the associated account's password (invalidating cached tickets via a subsequent krbtgt-relative change), and investigate the host for further compromise indicators.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires Sysmon or equivalent EDR file-creation telemetry; not observable from default Windows Security event logging.

title: SAMR Remote Enumeration at Scale from a Single Source
description: Detects an unusually high volume of Security Account Manager Remote (SAMR) protocol queries against a domain controller from a single source — consistent with tooling (e.g. enum4linux, NetSess, PowerView's Get-NetLocalGroupMember, or CrackMapExec) enumerating local group membership, user accounts, or domain policy remotely as a precursor to password-spray target selection or lateral-movement planning.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: DC security event log, Event ID 4661 (a handle to an object was requested) for the SAMR named pipe, grouped by source.

detection_logic: Event ID 4661 where Object_Name references the SAMR interface, grouped by IpAddress over 15 minutes; alert when count exceeds a per-source baseline.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4661 Object_Name="*SAMR*"
| bucket _time span=15m
| stats count as samr_requests by _time, IpAddress
| lookup samr_baseline.csv IpAddress OUTPUT baseline_max
| where samr_requests > baseline_max
tuning_guidance: Requires object-access auditing on the SAMR interface, which may need supplementing with the RestrictRemoteSAM hardening policy's audit mode or a network-layer SMB/RPC sensor if native event coverage is insufficient — validate against the deployed configuration. Maintain samr_baseline.csv for known legitimate management/monitoring sources.
investigation_steps: Identify the source host and account.
Check for known enumeration-tooling process indicators on the source.
Review whether this precedes a subsequent password-spray or brute-force attempt (correlate AD-AUTH namespace).
response_guidance: Investigate the source for compromise; consider tightening the RestrictRemoteSAM policy if broad anonymous/authenticated-user SAMR access is not required.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: SAMR access auditing detail varies by DC configuration and may require the RestrictRemoteSAM policy's audit capability or supplementary network-layer visibility; validate field/event availability against the deployed configuration.

title: Cleartext Password Observed in Process Command-Line Arguments
description: Detects a process command line containing syntax consistent with an embedded cleartext password — 'net use ... /user: ... [password]', 'runas /savecred', or 'schtasks /create ... /ru ... /rp [password]'. Command lines are visible to any process capable of enumerating the process list (and are historically logged in various places), so embedding a password directly on the command line is a common but risky administrative practice that exposes credentials to any user or process capable of viewing running command lines.

data_sources.name: Sysmon Event ID 1
data_sources.description: Process creation where CommandLine matches known cleartext-password argument patterns for net.exe, runas.exe, or schtasks.exe.

detection_logic: Sysmon Event ID 1 where Image matches net.exe/schtasks.exe and CommandLine includes '/user:' or '/rp' followed by an argument not matching a placeholder/prompt pattern.
spl:
index=sysmon sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1
| where match(Image, "(?i)(net(1)?|schtasks)\.exe$") AND (match(CommandLine, "(?i)/user:\S+\s+\S+") OR match(CommandLine, "(?i)/rp\s+\S+"))
| table _time, dvc, User, Image, CommandLine
tuning_guidance: Requires Sysmon or equivalent EDR command-line telemetry. Command-line-visible passwords are commonly used in legitimate (if poor-practice) scripting — expect meaningful noise and treat as a hygiene/awareness signal to drive remediation of the underlying scripts rather than a strictly malicious-only indicator.
investigation_steps: Identify the script/process source and the account whose credential was exposed.
Rotate the exposed credential.
Work with the script owner to eliminate the command-line credential exposure (e.g. via a credential-manager/vault reference instead).
response_guidance: Rotate the exposed credential and remediate the source script's practice regardless of whether the specific instance was malicious.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires Sysmon or equivalent EDR command-line telemetry; not observable from default Windows Security event logging.

title: Unattended Installation Answer File Accessed
description: Detects access to a Windows unattended-installation answer file (unattend.xml, sysprep.inf, or similar) in a well-known deployment-share location. These files historically embed local Administrator or domain-join credentials in plaintext or weakly obfuscated Base64 form, and are a well-documented credential-exposure source when left accessible on network shares or in leftover local file-system locations after imaging.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: File-system auditing Event ID 4663 on files named unattend.xml, sysprep.inf, or autounattend.xml.

detection_logic: Event ID 4663 where Object_Name matches 'unattend.xml', 'autounattend.xml', or 'sysprep.inf', from an account outside the expected imaging/deployment team.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4663 (Object_Name="*unattend.xml" OR Object_Name="*autounattend.xml" OR Object_Name="*sysprep.inf")
| lookup imaging_deployment_accounts.csv Subject_Account_Name OUTPUT is_expected
| where isnull(is_expected)
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_Name
