tuning_guidance: Requires SACL auditing on deployment-share/imaging locations. This is primarily a hygiene control — the durable fix is removing embedded credentials from these files and restricting share access, which also renders the detection largely moot once remediated.
investigation_steps: Determine whether the file contains embedded credentials.
If so, rotate them and remove the credential from the file.
response_guidance: Rotate any exposed credential and remediate the deployment process to avoid embedding credentials in these files going forward.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: SeDebugPrivilege Used by a Non-Standard Process to Access LSASS
description: Detects a process enabling SeDebugPrivilege (a privilege normally reserved for debuggers and a small set of system tools) and subsequently opening a handle to lsass.exe. Enabling this privilege is a required precursor step for most user-mode LSASS-dumping tools to obtain the necessary access rights, making the privilege-enable-then-LSASS-access sequence a useful, tool-agnostic detection signature.
required_log_sources: Windows Security Event Log (all domain-joined hosts)

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: Security event log, Event ID 4703 (a token right was adjusted) for SeDebugPrivilege followed by a process-access event against lsass.exe.

detection_logic: Event ID 4703 where the enabled privilege includes SeDebugPrivilege, from a Process_Name not in a recognized system/security-tooling allowlist, followed within a short window by process-access to lsass.exe.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4703
| search Privileges="*SeDebugPrivilege*"
| lookup edr_agent_processes.csv Process_Name OUTPUT is_expected
| where isnull(is_expected)
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Process_Name
tuning_guidance: Requires Privilege Use auditing (Audit Sensitive Privilege Use) enabled, which can be verbose domain-wide — consider scoping to Tier-0 and high-value endpoint segments first. Maintain edr_agent_processes.csv to exclude legitimate debugging/security tooling.
investigation_steps: Identify the process and confirm whether it subsequently accessed lsass.exe (correlate with AD-DC-008/AD-CRED-004 patterns for the specific access).
Treat as a probable credential-dumping precursor if the process is unrecognized.
response_guidance: Investigate and isolate the host if a credential-dumping tool is confirmed; treat as equivalent priority to a direct LSASS-access finding.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Remote Registry Access to a Workstation's SAM Hive
description: Detects a remote connection to the Remote Registry service targeting a workstation's or server's SAM hive from a source other than the host itself or recognized management tooling — the network-based variant of local SAM dumping, used to extract local account hashes from a remote machine without needing interactive or PSExec-style code execution on the target.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: Target-host security event log, Event ID 5145 (network share object access) for the \\<host>\winreg pipe combined with SAM-key access, or Event ID 4657 for remote SAM registry access.

detection_logic: Event ID 5145 where Share_Name=\\*\IPC$ and Relative_Target_Name=winreg, combined with a subsequent registry-key access event referencing the SAM hive, from a source not in it_management_sources.csv.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=5145 Share_Name="*IPC$" Relative_Target_Name="winreg"
| lookup it_management_sources.csv IpAddress OUTPUT is_expected
| where isnull(is_expected)
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, IpAddress
tuning_guidance: Requires file-share/object-access auditing on the target host. Exclude known remote-management/monitoring platforms via it_management_sources.csv.
investigation_steps: Identify the source and its authorization for remote registry access to this host.
Assume the target's local SAM database is exposed if confirmed unauthorized.
response_guidance: Reset the target host's local Administrator password and investigate the source for compromise.

references.title: OS Credential Dumping: Security Account Manager

author: Threat Detection Library

title: Known Credential-Dumping Tool Binary Written to Disk
description: Detects a file matching known credential-dumping tool hashes/import-hashes (Mimikatz, ProcDump when used for LSASS dumping, Rubeus, SharpKatz, and similar) being written to disk, regardless of filename. This complements AD-CRED-005's command-line-pattern detection by catching tools invoked without a recognizable command-line syntax, or staged before execution.

data_sources.name: Sysmon Event ID 1/11
data_sources.description: File-creation/process-creation events where the file hash or imphash matches known_credential_tool_hashes.csv.

detection_logic: Sysmon Event ID 1 or 11 where the SHA256/imphash value is present in known_credential_tool_hashes.csv.
spl:
index=sysmon sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" (EventCode=1 OR EventCode=11)
| rex field=Hashes "SHA256=(?<sha256>[A-Fa-f0-9]{64})"
| lookup known_credential_tool_hashes.csv sha256 OUTPUT tool_name
| where isnotnull(tool_name)
| table _time, dvc, Image, sha256, tool_name
tuning_guidance: Requires Sysmon file/process hashing enabled plus a maintained known_credential_tool_hashes.csv; hash-based detection has an inherent staleness problem as tool builds change — treat as one layer among several (alongside AD-CRED-005's syntax-based detection and general EDR/AV signature coverage), not a complete standalone control.
investigation_steps: Confirm the tool's presence and whether it has been executed.
Assume the corresponding credential-access technique has been attempted.
response_guidance: Isolate the host, remove the tool, and follow the response procedure appropriate to the specific technique the tool implements.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires Sysmon file/process hashing plus a maintained hash-inventory lookup; hash-based detection is inherently subject to staleness as tool builds change and should be treated as one layer among several rather than a complete standalone control.

title: PowerShell Credential-Harvesting Cmdlet or Script Signature Observed
description: Detects PowerShell script-block content matching known credential-harvesting function/cmdlet names — Invoke-Mimikatz, Get-GPPPassword, Invoke-Kerberoast, Get-PassHashes, or similar PowerSploit/Empire-derived function names. Because PowerShell Script Block Logging captures the deobfuscated script content at execution time, this can catch credential-harvesting activity even when delivered via an obfuscated one-liner or downloaded dynamically.
required_log_sources: Windows PowerShell Operational Log (all domain-joined hosts)

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational
data_sources.description: PowerShell Script Block Logging, Event ID 4104, where ScriptBlockText matches known credential-harvesting function names.

detection_logic: Event ID 4104 where ScriptBlockText matches known credential-harvesting function/cmdlet name patterns.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational" EventCode=4104
| where match(ScriptBlockText, "(?i)(invoke-mimikatz|get-gpppassword|invoke-kerberoast|get-passhashes|invoke-dcsync|out-minidump)")
| table _time, dvc, ScriptBlockText
tuning_guidance: Requires PowerShell Script Block Logging enabled (see AD-DC-015/GPO deployment for enforcement) — a prerequisite this detection depends on and which an attacker disabling logging (AD-DC-015) would specifically defeat.
investigation_steps: Review the full script block for context and intent.
Identify the executing account and host.
Follow the response procedure for whichever specific credential-access technique the script implements.
response_guidance: Treat as an active, high-confidence credential-harvesting attempt; isolate the host and investigate the broader attack chain.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires PowerShell Script Block Logging (Event ID 4104) enabled domain-wide; an attacker who first disables this logging (AD-DC-015) defeats this detection, underscoring the importance of separately monitoring for logging-impairment attempts.

title: NTDS.dit or SYSTEM Hive Copy Staged in a Temporary or Downloads Directory
description: Detects a file matching the name pattern of a copied NTDS.dit, SAM, SECURITY, or SYSTEM hive being written to a non-standard location such as a temp folder, Downloads folder, or removable-media path — a strong indicator that a previously extracted database/hive copy (see AD-DC-006/007 and AD-CRED-001) is being staged for exfiltration off the original host.

data_sources.name: Sysmon Event ID 11
data_sources.description: File create events where TargetFilename matches ntds.dit/SAM/SECURITY/SYSTEM naming patterns outside their expected system directories.

detection_logic: Sysmon Event ID 11 where TargetFilename matches '*ntds.dit', '*\SAM', '*\SECURITY', or '*\SYSTEM' (case-insensitive, as a copied filename) and the path is under a Temp, Downloads, or removable-media directory.
spl:
index=sysmon sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=11
| where match(TargetFilename, "(?i)(ntds\.dit|\\SAM$|\\SECURITY$|\\SYSTEM$)")
| where match(TargetFilename, "(?i)(\\Temp\\|\\Downloads\\|\\Desktop\\|[D-Z]:\\)")
| table _time, dvc, Image, TargetFilename
tuning_guidance: Requires Sysmon file-monitoring telemetry. Alert on all matches without exception; there is no legitimate reason for these files to be staged outside their expected system locations.
investigation_steps: Assume the staged database/hive has been fully exfiltrated or is about to be.
Identify the destination (network transfer, removable media, cloud upload) if possible.
Treat as a confirmed full domain-credential-database compromise if the file is ntds.dit.
response_guidance: Delete the staged file, block egress from the host immediately, and treat as equivalent severity to a confirmed DCSync/NTDS.dit exfiltration — follow full domain-compromise incident response.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires Sysmon or equivalent EDR file-creation telemetry; not observable from default Windows Security event logging.

title: Overpass-the-Hash Indicator via Unusual Ticket-Requesting Tool
description: Detects Kerberos TGT-request activity (4768) immediately preceded by process-creation evidence of an NTLM-hash-to-Kerberos-ticket conversion tool (e.g. Rubeus asktgt /rc4:, or Mimikatz sekurlsa::pth with a Kerberos-aware follow-on) on the requesting host — a broader, tool-execution-anchored companion to AD-KRB-023's ticket-behavior-only detection, adding process-level context that raises confidence when EDR/Sysmon telemetry is available.

data_sources.name: Sysmon Event ID 1
data_sources.description: Process creation matching Overpass-the-Hash tool syntax, correlated with a subsequent Event ID 4768 TGT request from the same host.

detection_logic: Sysmon Event ID 1 matching '/rc4:' or '/aes256:' ticket-request syntax followed within 5 minutes by an Event ID 4768 from the same host.
spl:
index=sysmon sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1
| where match(CommandLine, "(?i)(/rc4:|/aes256:|/aes128:).*asktgt")
| eval etype="opth_tool"
| append [
    search index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4768
    | eval etype="tgt_request"
    | rename Computer as dvc
  ]
| transaction dvc maxspan=5m startswith=eval(etype="opth_tool") endswith=eval(etype="tgt_request")
| where eventcount=2
| table _time, dvc, duration
tuning_guidance: Requires Sysmon or equivalent EDR command-line telemetry in addition to standard DC Kerberos auditing. Alert on all matches without exception.
investigation_steps: Identify the associated account and assume its NTLM hash has been compromised.
Review what the resulting TGT was subsequently used to access.
response_guidance: Reset the associated account's password immediately and investigate the host for the source of the compromised hash.

references.title: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Hash

author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires Sysmon or equivalent EDR command-line telemetry in addition to standard Kerberos event auditing; this tool-execution-anchored variant complements but does not replace AD-KRB-023's ticket-behavior-only detection, which functions without EDR telemetry.

title: Multiple Distinct Credential-Access Techniques Observed from the Same Host (Chain)
description: The flagship credential-access chain for this namespace: two or more distinct credential-access techniques (SAM hive save, LSASS dump, ticket export, DPAPI theft, credential-dumping tool execution) are observed from the same host within a short window. Attackers frequently attempt multiple extraction techniques in sequence, either because the first attempt failed (e.g. blocked by LSA Protection) or to maximize the amount of credential material obtained in a single compromised session — the combination is a significantly higher-confidence indicator of active, deliberate credential harvesting than any single technique alone.

data_sources.name: Sysmon Event ID 1/11
data_sources.description: Correlating distinct credential-access indicator event types (AD-CRED-001/004/005/009/015) by host within a short window.

detection_logic: Two or more distinct AD-CRED namespace matches (AD-CRED-001, 002, 003, 004, 005, 009, 015, 017) from the same dvc within 4 hours.
spl:
index=sysmon sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" (EventCode=1 OR EventCode=11)
| eval cred_category=case(
    match(CommandLine, "(?i)reg\.exe") AND match(CommandLine, "(?i)save"), "sam_hive_save",
    match(CommandLine, "(?i)comsvcs\.dll") AND match(CommandLine, "(?i)minidump"), "lsass_dump",
    match(CommandLine, "(?i)(sekurlsa::|lsadump::|kerberos::)"), "dumping_tool_syntax",
    match(TargetFilename, "(?i)\.kirbi$"), "ticket_export",
    true(), null()
  )
| where isnotnull(cred_category)
| bucket _time span=4h
| stats dc(cred_category) as distinct_techniques values(cred_category) as techniques by _time, dvc
| where distinct_techniques >= 2
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches without exception; requires Sysmon or equivalent EDR telemetry across the correlated event types.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed, active, thorough credential-harvesting session on the host.
Enumerate every account whose credential material may have been exposed via any of the matched techniques.
Isolate the host for full forensic investigation.
response_guidance: Isolate the host immediately, reset every credential potentially exposed (interactive sessions, cached domain credentials, any exported material), and treat as a confirmed active compromise requiring full incident response.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires Sysmon or equivalent EDR process-creation and file-creation telemetry across all correlated sub-detections; not achievable from default Windows Security event logging alone.

title: Service Account Credential Embedded in a Discovered Script or Scheduled Task
description: Detects file-access activity against a script (.ps1, .bat, .vbs) or scheduled-task definition that a periodic content-scanning process has flagged as containing an embedded plaintext service-account credential. This is a hygiene-oriented detection: the underlying risk is the credential being embedded at all, and this detection surfaces both the exposure itself and any subsequent access to the file by a principal other than its expected owner.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: File-system auditing Event ID 4663 correlated against a periodic script-content credential scan flagging files with embedded plaintext credentials.

detection_logic: Event ID 4663 on a file present in flagged_credential_scripts.csv (populated by a periodic out-of-band content-scanning process) accessed by an account other than the file's documented owner.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4663
| lookup flagged_credential_scripts.csv Object_Name OUTPUT expected_owner, embedded_account
| where isnotnull(embedded_account) AND Subject_Account_Name!=expected_owner
| table _time, dvc, Subject_Account_Name, Object_Name, embedded_account
tuning_guidance: Requires a companion out-of-band script-content scanning process feeding flagged_credential_scripts.csv — this detection cannot identify embedded credentials from file-access telemetry alone. The durable fix is removing the embedded credential and migrating to a credential vault/gMSA.
investigation_steps: Identify the embedded account and rotate its credential.
Work with the script owner to eliminate the embedded credential.
Review who accessed the file and whether they had a legitimate reason to.
response_guidance: Rotate the exposed service-account credential and remediate the script to remove the embedded plaintext value.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires a companion out-of-band script/task content-scanning process to identify embedded credentials; file-access telemetry alone cannot detect the presence of an embedded credential.

title: VPN Authentication Immediately Followed by Privileged AD Group Escalation
description: Detects a remote-access VPN authentication followed shortly afterward by the same identity being added to a Tier-0 AD group (Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, or equivalent). This chain covers the common external-compromise pattern where an attacker obtains VPN credentials (phishing, credential stuffing, or a purchased access broker listing), establishes a network foothold, and then rapidly escalates to full domain privilege using an ACL-abuse or credential-theft path already present in the environment.

data_sources.name: vpn_auth_log
data_sources.description: VPN gateway successful-authentication events (vendor-specific — e.g. Fortinet FortiGate SSL-VPN, Cisco AnyConnect, Palo Alto GlobalProtect).

detection_logic: A successful VPN authentication event for a user identity followed within 2 hours by an AD-GRP-001/003/004 (privileged-group-add) match for the same identity.
spl:
index=vpn sourcetype="vpn:auth" action="success"
| eval etype="vpn_auth"
| append [
    search index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" (EventCode=4728 OR EventCode=4732)
    | lookup tier0_privileged_groups.csv group_dn AS Group_Name OUTPUT is_tier0_group
    | where is_tier0_group=1
    | eval etype="privileged_group_add"
    | rename Member_Name as user
  ]
| transaction user maxspan=2h startswith=eval(etype="vpn_auth") endswith=eval(etype="privileged_group_add")
| where eventcount=2
| table _time, user, src_ip, duration
tuning_guidance: Field names and sourcetype vary significantly by VPN vendor (Fortinet, Cisco, Palo Alto, etc.) — adapt to the environment's actual VPN log schema before deployment. Alert on all matches once adapted.
investigation_steps: Identify the VPN source IP/geolocation and compare against the user's normal access pattern.
Determine how the VPN-authenticated identity obtained rights to escalate itself or was escalated by another actor.
Treat as an active external-to-domain-compromise chain.
response_guidance: Disable the VPN account and the escalated AD account immediately, remove the unauthorized group membership, and initiate full incident response assuming external initial access has led to domain compromise.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: VPN log field names, sourcetypes, and available identity-correlation fields vary significantly by vendor; the SPL shown is illustrative and must be adapted to the deployed VPN platform's actual schema.

title: RDP Session to a Domain-Joined Host Immediately Followed by Kerberoasting Activity
description: Detects an RDP logon to a domain-joined workstation or server (see the companion Windows RDP catalogue) followed shortly afterward by Kerberoasting-pattern ticket-request activity (AD-KRB-009/010) originating from that same account and source. This chain identifies the specific point where RDP-based lateral movement pivots into an AD credential-access technique, combining evidence from two separate log sources that are rarely correlated directly.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: Target-host RDP logon event (4624 Logon_Type=10) correlated with subsequent Kerberoasting-pattern ticket requests from the same account on the DC.

detection_logic: Event ID 4624 Logon_Type=10 (RDP) on any domain-joined host, followed within 1 hour by an AD-KRB-009/010 match (many-SPN or RC4-Kerberoasting pattern) for the same Account_Name.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10
| eval etype="rdp_logon"
| append [
    search index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4769 Ticket_Encryption_Type=0x17
    | bucket _time span=30m
    | stats dc(Service_Name) as spn_count by _time, Account_Name
    | where spn_count >= 5
    | eval etype="kerberoasting_pattern"
  ]
| transaction Account_Name maxspan=1h startswith=eval(etype="rdp_logon") endswith=eval(etype="kerberoasting_pattern")
| where eventcount=2
| table _time, Account_Name, Source_Network_Address, duration
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches; this correlation significantly raises confidence over either signal alone since Kerberoasting immediately following an interactive RDP session to a new host is a well-established lateral-movement/credential-access pivot pattern.
investigation_steps: Identify the RDP source and the account used.
Review which SPNs were targeted and whether any offline cracking succeeded (correlate subsequent authentication as the cracked service account).
response_guidance: Treat as an active lateral-movement-to-credential-access chain; reset any service accounts whose SPNs were targeted and investigate the RDP source for the initial compromise.

references.title: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Kerberoasting

author: Threat Detection Library

title: vCenter Snapshot or Clone Taken of a Virtualized Domain Controller
description: Detects a VMware vCenter snapshot or clone operation targeting a virtual machine known to be a domain controller. Because a VM-level snapshot or clone captures the entire disk image — including the live NTDS.dit database and registry hives — without requiring any access to the guest OS at all, this bypasses every guest-level DC hardening and monitoring control covered elsewhere in this catalogue (AD-DC-005/006/007) and hands an attacker with only vCenter/hypervisor access a complete offline copy of the domain database.

data_sources.name: vcenter_events
data_sources.description: vCenter task/event log for CreateSnapshot_Task or CloneVM_Task targeting a VM in dc_virtual_machine_inventory.csv.

detection_logic: vCenter event for CreateSnapshot_Task or CloneVM_Task where vm_name is present in dc_virtual_machine_inventory.csv (a maintained mapping of DC computer names to their virtual-machine names).
spl:
index=vcenter sourcetype="vmware:vcenter:events" (task_name="CreateSnapshot_Task" OR task_name="CloneVM_Task")
| lookup dc_virtual_machine_inventory.csv vm_name OUTPUT is_dc_vm
| where is_dc_vm=1
| table _time, vm_name, task_name, user
tuning_guidance: Requires the VMware Aria/vCenter event catalogue's logging integration and a maintained dc_virtual_machine_inventory.csv mapping DC hostnames to VM names — see the companion VMware Aria detection catalogue's equivalent snapshot-monitoring detections for the vSphere-side view of this same risk. Alert on all matches unless the operation matches a documented, approved DC-backup snapshot window.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a documented, approved backup/snapshot schedule for the DC VM.
Identify the destination of any clone operation and who has access to it.
If unauthorized, treat the DC's entire credential database as exfiltrated.
response_guidance: If unauthorized, treat as equivalent severity to a confirmed NTDS.dit theft — execute krbtgt double-reset and domain-wide credential rotation, and restrict vCenter access to the DC VM to the smallest possible administrative group.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires vCenter event-log integration and a maintained VM-to-DC-hostname inventory lookup; this detection targets the hypervisor-level view of the same underlying risk covered by the companion VMware Aria detection catalogue.

title: Backup Infrastructure Access Followed by NTDS.dit Extraction Indicator
description: Detects authentication to backup management infrastructure (e.g. Veeam Backup & Replication console, Windows Server Backup admin interface) followed shortly afterward by a restore or mount operation targeting a domain-controller backup job. Backup platforms are a frequently under-monitored path to NTDS.dit access, since they are specifically designed to provide full-system restore capability and are often exempted from the access controls applied to production DC infrastructure directly.

data_sources.name: backup_platform_audit
data_sources.description: Backup solution's own audit/activity log for console authentication and restore/mount operations (vendor-specific — Veeam, Commvault, Windows Server Backup, etc.).

detection_logic: Backup-platform authentication event followed within 1 hour by a restore or file-level-recovery/mount action against a backup job covering a domain controller (per dc_backup_jobs.csv), from an account not in authorized_backup_operators.csv.
spl:
index=backup sourcetype="backup:audit" action="restore" OR action="mount"
| lookup dc_backup_jobs.csv job_name OUTPUT covers_dc
| where covers_dc=1
| lookup authorized_backup_operators.csv user OUTPUT is_authorized
| where isnull(is_authorized)
| table _time, user, job_name, action
tuning_guidance: Backup platform log schemas vary significantly by vendor; adapt field names and sourcetypes to the deployed solution before relying on this detection. Maintain dc_backup_jobs.csv and authorized_backup_operators.csv accurately.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a documented DR-test or legitimate restore need.
Identify the restore destination and whether file-level access to ntds.dit specifically occurred.
Treat as equivalent to AD-DC-025/AD-CRED-017 if the restore output was subsequently accessed at the file level.
response_guidance: If unauthorized, treat as a probable NTDS.dit exfiltration via the backup platform and follow full domain-compromise incident response; restrict backup-console access and enforce MFA on the backup platform itself.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Backup-platform audit log schemas vary significantly by vendor (Veeam, Commvault, Windows Server Backup, etc.); the SPL shown is illustrative and must be adapted to the deployed solution's actual logging format.

title: HPE iLO or Dell iDRAC Out-of-Band Access to a Domain Controller's Physical Host
description: Detects an out-of-band management session (HPE iLO or Dell iDRAC virtual console/virtual media) established against the physical host underlying a domain controller. Out-of-band management provides console-level access below the OS — including the ability to mount virtual media and boot into an alternate OS to read the disk offline — completely bypassing every Windows-level detection in this catalogue (AD-DC namespace, LSA Protection, audit policy, EDR) since none of them are running yet at that point.

data_sources.name: ilo_idrac_events
data_sources.description: Out-of-band management controller authentication and virtual-console/virtual-media session events (see the companion HPE iLO and Dell iDRAC detection catalogues).

detection_logic: An iLO/iDRAC virtual-console or virtual-media session-start event where target_host maps (via dc_physical_host_inventory.csv) to a server hosting a domain controller, from an account not in authorized_oob_admins.csv.
spl:
(index=ilo sourcetype="hpe:ilo:event") OR (index=idrac sourcetype="dell:idrac:event")
| search action="virtual_console_start" OR action="virtual_media_mount"
| lookup dc_physical_host_inventory.csv target_host OUTPUT hosts_dc
| where hosts_dc=1
| lookup authorized_oob_admins.csv user OUTPUT is_authorized
| where isnull(is_authorized)
| table _time, user, target_host, action
tuning_guidance: Requires the companion HPE iLO and/or Dell iDRAC detection catalogue's logging integration plus a maintained dc_physical_host_inventory.csv mapping physical hosts to the DCs they run (whether bare-metal or as a hypervisor host for a virtualized DC). Alert on all matches for unauthorized access.
investigation_steps: Confirm against a documented, approved out-of-band maintenance window.
Review the specific virtual-console/media actions taken during the session.
If unauthorized, treat the DC as having potentially been accessed entirely outside OS-level monitoring.
response_guidance: If unauthorized, treat as a severe compromise with unknown scope (since OS-level telemetry cannot confirm what occurred below the OS) and restrict out-of-band management access to the smallest possible group with MFA enforced.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires integration with the companion HPE iLO and Dell iDRAC detection catalogues' logging plus a maintained physical-host-to-DC inventory; out-of-band access occurs below the OS and is inherently invisible to every Windows-level detection in the rest of this catalogue.

title: Rogue DHCP Server Correlated with Subsequent AD Credential-Relay Activity
description: Detects a rogue/unauthorized DHCP server being identified on the network (see the companion Windows DHCP detection catalogue) followed within a short window by NTLM-relay-pattern indicators (AD-NTLM-007/008/009) against the domain. A rogue DHCP server is a classic staging step for a broader adversary-in-the-middle position, since it lets an attacker redirect DNS/gateway settings for a subnet segment and intercept or relay authentication traffic that would otherwise reach the legitimate DC directly.

data_sources.name: dhcp_rogue_detection
data_sources.description: Rogue DHCP server detection event from the companion Windows DHCP detection catalogue.

detection_logic: A rogue-DHCP-server detection event followed within 2 hours by an AD-NTLM-007/008/009 match (NTLM relay pattern) sourced from the same subnet.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:DHCP-Audit" event_type="rogue_server_detected"
| eval etype="rogue_dhcp"
| append [
    search index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4624 Authentication_Package="NTLM"
    | eval etype="ntlm_relay_pattern"
  ]
| transaction subnet maxspan=2h startswith=eval(etype="rogue_dhcp") endswith=eval(etype="ntlm_relay_pattern")
| where eventcount=2
| table _time, rogue_server_ip, subnet, duration
tuning_guidance: Requires the companion Windows DHCP detection catalogue's rogue-server detection and a shared subnet field for correlation; treat as a supporting, moderate-confidence indicator given the indirect subnet-level correlation rather than a direct causal link.
investigation_steps: Locate and remove the rogue DHCP server.
Review which hosts on the affected subnet received configuration from it.
Assess whether any authentication traffic was actually intercepted/relayed.
response_guidance: Remove the rogue DHCP server, enforce DHCP snooping/802.1X on the affected subnet, and treat any NTLM relay activity from the same window with the same urgency as AD-NTLM-007.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires integration with the companion Windows DHCP detection catalogue's rogue-server detection; the subnet-level correlation to NTLM relay activity is indirect and should be treated as a supporting signal.

title: Fortinet VPN Brute-Force Success Correlated with AD Lateral Movement
description: Detects a successful authentication following a brute-force/spray pattern on a Fortinet SSL-VPN (see the companion Fortinet detection catalogue) for an identity that also holds a domain account, followed by that domain account's first-ever authentication to a new internal host. This chain identifies the specific transition point from external network-perimeter compromise to internal AD-based lateral movement.

data_sources.name: fortigate_vpn_auth
data_sources.description: FortiGate SSL-VPN authentication events from the companion Fortinet detection catalogue's brute-force/spray-success detections.

detection_logic: A Fortinet VPN spray/brute-force-success detection match for a user identity followed within 4 hours by an AD-AUTH-030 (first-seen-source, impossible-travel, or new-host-first-authentication) match for the corresponding domain account.
spl:
index=fortigate sourcetype="fortigate:vpn" logdesc="sslvpn login" status="success"
| eval etype="vpn_success"
| append [
    search index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4624
    | lookup ad_privileged_src_baseline.csv Account_Name, dvc OUTPUT is_baseline
    | where isnull(is_baseline)
    | eval etype="new_host_auth"
    | rename Account_Name as user
  ]
| transaction user maxspan=4h startswith=eval(etype="vpn_success") endswith=eval(etype="new_host_auth")
| where eventcount=2
| table _time, user, srcip, duration
tuning_guidance: Requires the companion Fortinet detection catalogue's VPN brute-force/spray detections and a shared user-identity field between the VPN and AD logs (typically UPN or sAMAccountName). Alert on all matches once field mapping is confirmed accurate for the environment.
investigation_steps: Confirm the VPN brute-force finding preceded genuine unauthorized access rather than a legitimate user's own retry.
Review the full scope of internal hosts accessed following the VPN authentication.
response_guidance: Disable the compromised account, terminate the VPN session, and investigate the full extent of internal lateral movement.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires integration with the companion Fortinet detection catalogue's VPN brute-force/spray detections and a reliable shared-identity field between the VPN and AD log sources.

title: Break-Glass Account Used Across Multiple Platforms Within a Short Window
description: Detects a designated break-glass/emergency-access identity being used to authenticate to AD (AD-PERSIST-015) and to at least one other Tier-0 platform covered elsewhere in this library (vCenter, iLO/iDRAC, Fortinet management, Splunk Platform admin) within a short window, without a corresponding declared-emergency record. Coordinated cross-platform break-glass use is a high-confidence indicator of a sophisticated attacker who has specifically identified and targeted these normally-excluded-from-MFA accounts as a way to move across every Tier-0 system in the environment with minimal friction.

data_sources.name: breakglass_accounts.csv
data_sources.description: Cross-platform inventory of designated break-glass/emergency-access identities and their corresponding account name on each platform.

detection_logic: Two or more distinct platform authentication events for accounts mapped to the same break-glass identity in breakglass_accounts.csv within 24 hours, with no matching entry in declared_emergency_events.csv.
spl:
(index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4624) OR (index=vcenter sourcetype="vmware:vcenter:events" task_name="Login") OR (index=ilo OR index=idrac) OR (index=fortigate sourcetype="fortigate:event" logdesc="admin login") OR (index=_audit sourcetype="audittrail")
| lookup breakglass_accounts.csv platform_account AS user OUTPUT breakglass_identity, platform
| where isnotnull(breakglass_identity)
| lookup declared_emergency_events.csv breakglass_identity OUTPUT window_start, window_end
| where isnull(window_start) OR _time < window_start OR _time > window_end
| bucket _time span=24h
| stats dc(platform) as platform_count values(platform) as platforms by _time, breakglass_identity
| where platform_count >= 2
tuning_guidance: Requires a maintained cross-platform breakglass_accounts.csv mapping each platform's local account name to a shared break-glass identity, and a declared_emergency_events.csv process for logging legitimate use. Alert on all matches.
investigation_steps: Immediately contact the account custodian(s) to confirm whether a genuine, undeclared emergency is underway.
Review session activity on every platform where the identity was used.
response_guidance: If unauthorized, treat as an active, sophisticated Tier-0 compromise spanning multiple platforms; reset every corresponding account's credentials and review activity on each platform in full.
author: Threat Detection Library
performance_guidance: This correlation spans multiple index sources across every catalogue in the library; run as a scheduled correlation search rather than real-time to manage cost.
attack_mapping_note: Requires a maintained cross-platform break-glass account inventory and a shared identity-mapping field across every catalogue's log sources in this library; the SPL shown is illustrative and must be adapted to each platform's actual field names.

title: Identity-Focused Ransomware Chain: Mass Privilege Escalation, Mass Lockout, and Backup Deletion
description: The flagship identity-ransomware/destructive-attack chain: detects the specific combination of (1) a privileged-account compromise indicator (AD-GRP-006/AD-DELEG-008/AD-REPL-002 or similar), (2) a mass account-lockout or mass-password-reset event (AD-USER-014/016 or AD-AUTH-015), and (3) a backup-deletion or shadow-copy-deletion indicator, occurring within a short overall window. This combination is the well-documented pre-encryption playbook used by modern ransomware operators: escalate to Domain Admin, lock out legitimate administrators and disable recovery options, delete backups/shadow copies to prevent restoration, and only then deploy the encryption payload — detecting this chain before the final encryption step is the highest-value intervention point available anywhere in this library.
required_log_sources: Windows Security Event Log (all domain-joined hosts)

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: Correlated privilege-escalation, mass-lockout, and backup/shadow-copy-deletion indicators across the domain.

detection_logic: A privileged-group-add or DCSync-chain match, combined with a mass-lockout/mass-password-reset match, combined with vssadmin/wbadmin delete-shadow or backup-deletion evidence, all within a 12-hour window.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" (EventCode=4728 OR EventCode=4732 OR EventCode=4740 OR EventCode=4724)
| eval stage=case(
    (EventCode=4728 OR EventCode=4732), "privilege_escalation",
    EventCode=4740, "mass_lockout",
    EventCode=4724, "mass_password_reset",
    true(), null()
  )
| append [
    search (index=sysmon sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1)
    | where match(CommandLine, "(?i)(vssadmin.*delete.*shadow|wbadmin.*delete.*catalog|wmic.*shadowcopy.*delete)")
    | eval stage="backup_deletion"
  ]
| where isnotnull(stage)
| bucket _time span=12h
| stats dc(stage) as stage_count values(stage) as stages_observed by _time
| where stage_count >= 3
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches without exception and route to the highest-urgency incident-response paging tier available — this chain represents the last practical detection opportunity before ransomware encryption begins in a well-executed identity-based attack.
investigation_steps: Treat as an active ransomware pre-encryption sequence in progress — do not wait for further confirmation before beginning containment.
Identify every host touched by the actor(s) involved in any matched stage.
Isolate network segments proactively while investigation continues.
response_guidance: Immediately engage full incident response: isolate affected systems from the network, disable the compromised privileged account(s), verify offline/immutable backup integrity, and assume encryption deployment is imminent or already underway.
author: Threat Detection Library
performance_guidance: Run as a scheduled correlation search given the multi-source, multi-stage nature of this detection; consider a shorter evaluation interval (e.g. every 15 minutes) given the extreme urgency of a true positive.

title: Domain Controller Destruction Chain: NTDS Access, Backup Deletion, and Service Impairment
description: Detects the specific combination of (1) NTDS/credential-database access (AD-DC-006/007), (2) backup or shadow-copy deletion, and (3) NTDS service impairment (AD-DC-005) targeting the same or related domain controllers within a short window — the signature of a deliberate DC-destruction attack aimed at permanently disabling AD authentication capability domain-wide, distinct from the credential-theft-focused chains elsewhere in this catalogue in that its goal is availability destruction rather than persistence or further escalation.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: Correlated NTDS-access, backup-deletion, and service-impairment indicators on domain controllers.

detection_logic: An AD-DC-006/007 match (VSS creation or NTDS.dit access) combined with backup-deletion command-line evidence and an AD-DC-005 match (NTDS service stopped), all on the same or a related DC within 6 hours.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:System" EventCode=7036 service_name="Active Directory Domain Services" service_state="stopped"
| eval stage="ntds_stopped"
| append [
    search index=sysmon sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1
    | where match(CommandLine, "(?i)(vssadmin.*delete.*shadow|wbadmin.*delete)")
    | eval stage="backup_deletion"
  ]
| append [
    search index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4663 Object_Name="*ntds.dit"
    | eval stage="ntds_access"
  ]
| lookup domain_controllers.csv computer_name AS dvc OUTPUT is_dc
| where is_dc=1
| bucket _time span=6h
| stats dc(stage) as stage_count values(stage) as stages by _time, dvc
| where stage_count >= 2
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches without exception; the combination of any two of these three stages on a DC within a short window has essentially no legitimate business explanation.
investigation_steps: Treat as an active DC-destruction attack in progress.
Verify replica health of every remaining domain controller immediately.
Confirm offline/immutable backup availability outside the affected environment.
response_guidance: Immediately isolate the affected DC(s), verify the domain retains sufficient healthy DC replicas to survive, restore service if the NTDS service was stopped maliciously, and engage full incident response assuming a deliberate availability attack.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Cross-Forest SIDHistory Escalation Correlated with Trust Weakening and Cross-Platform Privileged Access
description: Extends AD-TRUST-011's single-forest chain to explicitly correlate with subsequent cross-platform privileged access — an escalated SIDHistory-bearing identity authenticating not just within AD but to another Tier-0 platform (vCenter, Fortinet management, Splunk Platform admin) in the trusting forest shortly afterward. This confirms the escalation was not merely established but actively exploited to reach infrastructure beyond AD itself.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: AD-TRUST-011 match correlated with a subsequent cross-platform administrative authentication for the same escalated identity.

detection_logic: AD-TRUST-011 match followed within 4 hours by an administrative authentication event on vCenter, Splunk Platform, or another Tier-0 platform for the same account identity (via a cross-platform identity-mapping lookup).
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4716
| eval etype="trust_weakened"
| append [
    search index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" (EventCode=4768 OR EventCode=4769)
    | lookup sidhistory_inventory.csv account AS Account_Name OUTPUT sid_history_values
    | lookup privileged_rids.csv rid AS sid_history_values OUTPUT rid_group_name
    | where isnotnull(rid_group_name)
    | eval etype="privileged_sidhistory_auth"
  ]
| append [
    search index=vcenter sourcetype="vmware:vcenter:events" task_name="Login"
    | eval etype="cross_platform_admin_auth"
    | rename user as Account_Name
  ]
| transaction Account_Name maxspan=4h startswith=eval(etype="trust_weakened") endswith=eval(etype="cross_platform_admin_auth")
| where eventcount>=2
| table _time, Account_Name, duration
tuning_guidance: Requires a cross-platform identity-mapping lookup (e.g. UPN-to-vCenter-username) to correlate the escalated AD identity with its equivalent account on other Tier-0 platforms. Alert on all matches.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed, actively exploited cross-forest-to-cross-platform privilege escalation.
Enumerate every platform the escalated identity accessed.
response_guidance: Full cross-platform incident response: disable the trust, clear the SIDHistory value, force credential resets across every platform the identity accessed, and review all actions taken during each session.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires a maintained cross-platform identity-mapping lookup correlating the AD account with its equivalent identity on other Tier-0 platforms.

title: AD CS Certificate-Based Authentication Used to Access a Non-AD Tier-0 Platform
description: Detects a certificate issued under suspicious circumstances (AD-PERSIST-009) being used shortly afterward for authentication to a non-AD Tier-0 platform that trusts the same PKI (e.g. a VPN concentrator, Fortinet management interface, or Splunk Platform configured for certificate-based SSO). This extends AD CS abuse beyond AD authentication itself, since a compromised certificate template's blast radius includes every relying party that trusts the same certificate authority.

data_sources.name: cert_auth_correlation
data_sources.description: AD-PERSIST-009 match correlated with subsequent certificate-based authentication events on other PKI-trusting platforms.

detection_logic: AD-PERSIST-009 match followed within 24 hours by a certificate-based authentication event on a non-AD platform for the same identity.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4887
| lookup tier0_privileged_accounts.csv account AS SAN_UPN OUTPUT is_privileged_upn
| where is_privileged_upn=1
| eval etype="cert_issued"
| append [
    search index=vpn sourcetype="vpn:auth" auth_method="certificate"
    | eval etype="cert_platform_auth"
    | rename user as SAN_UPN
  ]
| transaction SAN_UPN maxspan=24h startswith=eval(etype="cert_issued") endswith=eval(etype="cert_platform_auth")
| where eventcount=2
| table _time, SAN_UPN, duration
tuning_guidance: Requires identifying every relying party in the environment that trusts the same PKI as AD (VPN, network device management, third-party SSO) and their respective log sources; the SPL shown illustrates the pattern for a certificate-authenticating VPN as one example.
investigation_steps: Same as AD-PERSIST-009's investigation steps, extended to review every relying-party platform the certificate could be used against.
Enumerate every platform that trusts the same PKI and check each for authentication using the flagged certificate.
response_guidance: Revoke the certificate across every relying party (not just AD), and audit each platform for unauthorized access performed using it.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires identifying and integrating with every relying party's log source that trusts the same PKI as AD; the SPL shown is illustrative for one example (certificate-authenticating VPN) and must be extended per environment.

title: Jump Host / PAW Compromise Correlated with Subsequent Privileged AD Session
description: Detects a compromise indicator on a designated jump host or Privileged Access Workstation (PAW) — such as a credential-dumping tool execution (AD-CRED-005) or an unrecognized process — followed by a privileged AD session originating from that same jump host/PAW. Since jump hosts and PAWs are specifically designated as the trusted source for privileged AD access throughout this catalogue's tuning guidance (many AD-AUTH/AD-GRP detections exempt jump-host-sourced privileged logons from alerting), a compromise of the jump host itself undermines that trust assumption and warrants its own dedicated detection.

data_sources.name: Sysmon Event ID 1
data_sources.description: Credential-dumping or unrecognized-process indicators on a host in jump_host_subnets.csv, correlated with subsequent privileged AD authentication from the same host.

detection_logic: An AD-CRED-005 match (or similar compromise indicator) on a host present in jump_host_subnets.csv/paw_inventory.csv, followed within 4 hours by a privileged AD-AUTH-019/020 (Domain Admin/Enterprise Admin logon) from the same host.
spl:
index=sysmon sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1
| lookup paw_inventory.csv dvc OUTPUT is_paw
| where is_paw=1
| where match(CommandLine, "(?i)(sekurlsa::|lsadump::|kerberos::|mimikatz)")
| eval etype="paw_compromise_indicator"
| append [
    search index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4624
    | lookup tier0_privileged_accounts.csv account AS Account_Name OUTPUT is_privileged
    | where is_privileged=1
    | lookup paw_inventory.csv Source_Network_Address OUTPUT is_paw_source
    | where is_paw_source=1
    | eval etype="privileged_ad_session"
    | rename Source_Network_Address as dvc
  ]
| transaction dvc maxspan=4h startswith=eval(etype="paw_compromise_indicator") endswith=eval(etype="privileged_ad_session")
| where eventcount=2
| table _time, dvc, duration
tuning_guidance: Requires accurate paw_inventory.csv/jump_host_subnets.csv and Sysmon coverage on these specifically hardened hosts (which should already have enhanced monitoring given their trust level). Alert on all matches without exception.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed PAW/jump-host compromise with subsequent privileged-session exposure.
Assume every privileged credential used from this host during the exposure window is compromised.
response_guidance: Isolate the jump host/PAW immediately, reset every privileged credential used from it since the compromise indicator, and rebuild the host from a known-good image before returning it to service.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Service Account Credential Reused Across AD and a Network Device Management Interface
description: Detects the same credential (identified by a shared username pattern) being used both for AD service-account authentication and for administrative access to a Fortinet network-device management interface. Credential reuse across a domain identity and network-infrastructure management is a common operational shortcut that, once compromised on either side, gives an attacker a pivot point between the identity plane and the network-infrastructure plane.

data_sources.name: shared_credential_correlation
data_sources.description: AD service-account authentication correlated with Fortinet management-interface authentication using a matching username pattern.

detection_logic: An AD service-account authentication event and a Fortinet management-interface authentication event within the same 1-hour window sharing an identical or pattern-matched username, where the account is not documented as an intentional shared-identity integration in shared_credential_inventory.csv.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4768
| lookup service_accounts.csv account AS Account_Name OUTPUT is_service_account
| where is_service_account=1
| eval etype="ad_service_auth"
| append [
    search index=fortigate sourcetype="fortigate:event" logdesc="admin login"
    | eval etype="fortigate_admin_auth"
    | rename user as Account_Name
  ]
| lookup shared_credential_inventory.csv Account_Name OUTPUT is_documented_shared
| where isnull(is_documented_shared)
| transaction Account_Name maxspan=1h
| where eventcount>=2
| table _time, Account_Name, duration
tuning_guidance: Requires a shared username-pattern match between AD and Fortinet identity spaces (often not a perfect match given differing naming conventions) and a maintained shared_credential_inventory.csv for known, intentional integrations (e.g. a RADIUS/LDAP-backed admin account). Route to a moderate-priority review queue given the inherent noise of pattern-based username matching.
investigation_steps: Confirm whether the credential reuse is a known, documented integration.
If not, treat as an unmanaged shared-credential risk and recommend separating the identities.
response_guidance: If unauthorized/undocumented, separate the credentials and rotate both; if a compromise is suspected on either platform, treat both as compromised.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Username-pattern matching across AD and Fortinet identity spaces is inherently approximate given differing naming conventions between platforms; this detection surfaces candidate shared-credential risk for review rather than a confirmed compromise.

title: Full Kill Chain: Kerberoasting → Pass-the-Hash → DCSync → Golden Ticket
description: The ultimate flagship chain in this catalogue: correlates the complete textbook AD compromise progression — Kerberoasting to obtain a service account's crackable hash, Pass-the-Hash or Overpass-the-Hash using that cracked/captured hash to authenticate further, DCSync using the resulting elevated access to pull the krbtgt hash, and finally Golden-Ticket-consistent ticket-lifetime anomalies indicating the krbtgt hash is now being used to forge tickets. Detecting any single stage is valuable; detecting the full sequence from the same actor is definitive confirmation of a complete, successful domain compromise and should trigger the highest-tier incident-response response available.

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: Correlated Kerberoasting, Pass-the-Hash/Overpass-the-Hash, DCSync, and Golden-Ticket-indicator events by actor/derived-identity across an extended window.

detection_logic: AD-KRB-010 (RC4-Kerberoasting) match, followed within 48 hours by an AD-KRB-023 (Overpass-the-Hash) or NTLM pass-the-hash-fan-out match involving a related identity, followed within a further 48 hours by an AD-REPL-001/002 (DCSync) match, followed by an AD-KRB-016/017 (Golden Ticket indicator) match — all within an overall 7-day window.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4769 Ticket_Encryption_Type=0x17
| bucket _time span=30m
| stats dc(Service_Name) as spn_count by _time, Account_Name
| where spn_count >= 5
| eval stage="1_kerberoasting"
| append [
    search index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4768
    | rex field="Certificate_Issuer_Name" "(?<opth_indicator>rc4)"
    | where isnotnull(opth_indicator)
    | eval stage="2_pass_or_overpass_the_hash"
  ]
| append [
    search index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4662
    | search Properties="*1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2*"
    | lookup domain_controllers.csv computer_name AS Subject_Account_Name OUTPUT is_dc
    | where isnull(is_dc)
    | eval stage="3_dcsync"
    | rename Subject_Account_Name as Account_Name
  ]
| append [
    search index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4769
    | where Ticket_Options="*forwardable*" AND Ticket_Lifetime>36000
    | eval stage="4_golden_ticket_indicator"
  ]
| bucket _time span=7d
| stats dc(stage) as stage_count values(stage) as stages_observed by _time
| where stage_count >= 3
tuning_guidance: Alert on all matches without exception and treat as the single highest-confidence, highest-urgency detection in the entire library — while the identity linkage across stages is necessarily approximate (the actor may deliberately use different accounts/hosts at each stage to evade simpler correlation), the combination of all four stages occurring within one domain in a single week has essentially no benign explanation.
investigation_steps: Treat as a confirmed, complete domain compromise — do not wait for further validation before beginning full incident response.
Reconstruct the full timeline across all four stages to identify the initial access vector.
Assume every credential in the domain is compromised via the krbtgt key.
response_guidance: Execute the full krbtgt double-reset procedure, reset every privileged account's password, rotate every service account credential, and engage the most senior incident-response resources available — this pattern represents complete, unrecoverable-without-remediation domain compromise.

references.title: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Golden Ticket

author: Threat Detection Library
performance_guidance: Run as a scheduled correlation search over an extended (multi-day) lookback window given the realistic timeline of a staged compromise; this is not intended as a sub-minute real-time search.
attack_mapping_note: Identity linkage across the four stages is necessarily approximate since a sophisticated actor may deliberately use different accounts or source hosts at each stage specifically to evade correlation; the value of this detection is in surfacing the combination of stages within one domain over a realistic compromise timeframe, not in proving a single unbroken identity chain.

title: Virtualized Domain Controller Console Access via Hypervisor Bypassing AD Authentication
description: Detects a vCenter/ESXi virtual-machine console (VMRC) session opened against a virtualized domain controller, without a corresponding OS-level interactive logon event on the DC itself in the same window. This gap indicates the attacker viewed or interacted with the DC's console at the hypervisor level (potentially resetting a local account, extracting information visible on-screen, or interacting with a boot-time recovery menu) in a way that OS-level Windows Security auditing cannot observe at all, since the console session bypasses the normal Windows logon path entirely.

data_sources.name: vcenter_events
data_sources.description: vCenter VMRC console-session-open event for a VM in dc_virtual_machine_inventory.csv, correlated against the DC's own Windows Security log for a lack of matching interactive-logon evidence.

detection_logic: A vCenter VMRC console-open event for a VM in dc_virtual_machine_inventory.csv with no corresponding Event ID 4624 Logon_Type=2 on the DC's own security log within the same session window.
spl:
index=vcenter sourcetype="vmware:vcenter:events" task_name="OpenConsole" OR event_type="*RemoteConsole*"
| lookup dc_virtual_machine_inventory.csv vm_name OUTPUT is_dc_vm, dc_hostname
| where is_dc_vm=1
| eval etype="vmrc_console_open"
| append [
    search index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=2
    | eval etype="os_interactive_logon"
    | rename dvc as dc_hostname
  ]
| transaction dc_hostname maxspan=15m
| where mvcount(etype)=1 AND etype="vmrc_console_open"
| table _time, vm_name, user, dc_hostname
tuning_guidance: Requires the companion VMware Aria/vCenter detection catalogue's console-session logging and a maintained dc_virtual_machine_inventory.csv. Alert on all matches for unauthorized console sessions; exclude documented, approved hypervisor-level maintenance windows (e.g. troubleshooting a hung boot).
investigation_steps: Confirm against a documented, approved console-access change ticket.
Review the vCenter session's actual actions if console recording/screenshot capability is available.
Treat the DC's local recovery/administrative capability as potentially exposed.
response_guidance: If unauthorized, treat as a severe compromise with limited forensic visibility into what occurred at the console; restrict VMRC console access to the DC VM to the smallest possible administrative group and consider requiring a documented change ticket for all future console sessions.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires integration with the companion VMware Aria/vCenter detection catalogue's console-session event logging and a maintained VM-to-DC-hostname inventory; console-level interaction visibility beyond session-open/close is generally limited without screen-recording capability.

title: Cloud Identity Provider Sign-In Anomaly Correlated with On-Premises AD Privileged Action
description: Detects a sign-in risk/anomaly flagged by a cloud identity provider (e.g. Entra ID/Azure AD Conditional Access risk detection, for a hybrid-identity environment synchronized from this AD) for an identity that also performs a privileged on-premises AD action shortly afterward. In hybrid-identity environments, cloud-side sign-in risk signals (impossible travel, anonymous-IP, leaked-credential match) are often the earliest available warning of a credential compromise that will subsequently manifest on-premises.
required_log_sources: Cloud Identity Provider sign-in log (e.g. Entra ID/Azure AD)

data_sources.name: cloud_identity_signin_log
data_sources.description: Cloud identity provider risk-flagged sign-in events for a hybrid-identity account, correlated with on-premises AD activity for the synchronized identity.

detection_logic: A cloud identity provider sign-in event flagged with elevated risk, followed within 4 hours by a privileged on-premises AD action (AD-GRP/AD-ACL/AD-DELEG namespace match) for the corresponding synchronized identity.
spl:
index=azuread sourcetype="azure:aad:signin" riskLevel IN ("medium","high")
| eval etype="cloud_risky_signin"
| append [
    search index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" (EventCode=4728 OR EventCode=4732 OR EventCode=5136)
    | eval etype="onprem_privileged_action"
    | rename Subject_Account_Name as user_principal_name
  ]
| transaction user_principal_name maxspan=4h startswith=eval(etype="cloud_risky_signin") endswith=eval(etype="onprem_privileged_action")
| where eventcount=2
| table _time, user_principal_name, risk_level, duration
tuning_guidance: Requires ingestion of the cloud identity provider's sign-in log (outside this library's native scope, but a common companion data source in hybrid-identity environments) and a reliable UPN-based identity mapping between the cloud and on-premises directories.
investigation_steps: Review the specific cloud risk signal (impossible travel, leaked credential, anonymous IP, etc.).
Assess whether the subsequent on-premises privileged action is consistent with the legitimate user's normal behavior.
response_guidance: If the cloud risk signal is confirmed genuine, treat the on-premises action as performed under a compromised identity; reset the account's password (which also invalidates on-premises Kerberos tickets) and review both cloud and on-premises activity.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires ingestion of a cloud identity provider's sign-in/risk log, which is outside this AD-focused catalogue's native Windows Security event scope but a common companion data source in hybrid-identity (Entra ID/Azure AD Connect-synchronized) environments.

title: SIEM/EDR Self-Protection Tampering Correlated with AD Audit-Policy Weakening
description: Detects tampering with Splunk Platform's own self-protection controls (see the companion Splunk Platform detection catalogue's SPL-SELF namespace — e.g. a universal forwarder being disabled, an index being deleted, or a correlation-search being disabled) occurring within a short window of an AD-DC-014 (audit policy weakened) or AD-DC-015 (PowerShell logging disabled) match. A sophisticated attacker aiming to operate undetected in AD will often target both the source telemetry (DC audit policy) and the downstream detection pipeline (the SIEM itself) together — this correlation raises confidence that logging degradation is a deliberate evasion campaign rather than an isolated administrative change.

data_sources.name: splunk_self_protection_events
data_sources.description: Companion Splunk Platform detection catalogue's self-protection tampering indicators (forwarder disablement, index deletion, correlation-search disablement).

detection_logic: An AD-DC-014 or AD-DC-015 match within 4 hours of a Splunk Platform self-protection tampering indicator from the companion catalogue's SPL-SELF namespace.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4719
| lookup domain_controllers.csv computer_name AS dvc OUTPUT is_dc
| where is_dc=1
| eval etype="ad_audit_weakened"
| append [
    search index=_audit sourcetype="audittrail" action="edit" object_type="correlationsearch" status="disabled"
    | eval etype="splunk_self_protection_tampered"
  ]
| transaction etype maxspan=4h startswith=eval(etype="ad_audit_weakened") endswith=eval(etype="splunk_self_protection_tampered")
| where eventcount=2
| table _time, duration
tuning_guidance: Requires the companion Splunk Platform detection catalogue's SPL-SELF namespace to be deployed and correlatable. Alert on all matches without exception.
investigation_steps: Treat as a deliberate, coordinated defense-evasion campaign targeting both source telemetry and the detection pipeline itself.
Restore both AD audit policy and the disabled Splunk self-protection controls immediately.
Assume a period of significantly degraded detection capability and increase manual review of activity during the exposure window.
response_guidance: Restore all tampered controls immediately, treat the exposure window as a high-risk investigative blind spot requiring compensating manual review, and engage incident response assuming a sophisticated, detection-aware attacker.
author: Threat Detection Library
attack_mapping_note: Requires the companion Splunk Platform detection catalogue's SPL-SELF (self-protection) namespace to be deployed in the same Splunk environment for correlation.

title: RDP Session Chain Across Multiple Hosts Culminating in Domain Controller Access
description: Detects a chain of RDP sessions (see the companion Windows RDP detection catalogue) hopping across multiple distinct hosts within a short window, culminating in an RDP or console session to a domain controller (AD-AUTH-023). Multi-hop RDP chaining is a classic manual lateral-movement pattern used to progressively reach higher-value targets from an initial foothold, and detecting the full chain — rather than just the final DC-access step — provides the complete path an attacker used to get there.
required_log_sources: Windows Security Event Log (all domain-joined hosts)

data_sources.name: WinEventLog:Security
data_sources.description: Chained RDP logon events (4624 Logon_Type=10) across multiple distinct source/destination host pairs for the same account, culminating in a DC destination.

detection_logic: Three or more Event ID 4624 Logon_Type=10 events for the same Account_Name across distinct destination hosts within 4 hours, where the final destination is a domain controller.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10
| sort 0 _time
| streamstats current=f window=1 last(dvc) as prev_hop by Account_Name
| lookup domain_controllers.csv computer_name AS dvc OUTPUT is_dc
| bucket _time span=4h
| stats dc(dvc) as hop_count, values(dvc) as hosts_visited, max(is_dc) as reached_dc by _time, Account_Name
| where hop_count >= 3 AND reached_dc=1
tuning_guidance: Exclude known jump-host/PAW-sourced administrative RDP chains via paw_inventory.csv/jump_host_subnets.csv, since a legitimate admin routing through an approved jump-host chain to a DC would otherwise match this pattern. Alert on all matches from non-approved sources.
investigation_steps: Reconstruct the full RDP hop chain and identify the initial source.
Review each intermediate host for compromise indicators.
Treat the DC as the terminus of an active lateral-movement campaign.
response_guidance: Isolate every host in the chain, reset the account's credentials, and treat the DC access as a confirmed Tier-0 compromise requiring full incident response.
author: Threat Detection Library

title: Coordinated Multi-Vendor Infrastructure Compromise Indicator Correlated Across the Detection Library
description: A broad-scope safety-net correlation: detects Tier-0-severity findings from three or more distinct catalogues in this library (AD, ESXi/vCenter, Red Hat, Fortinet, iDRAC, iLO, VCF, Splunk Platform) occurring within the same 24-hour window across the environment. While each individual catalogue's detections are designed to stand on their own, a well-resourced adversary conducting a full-environment compromise will typically generate findings across multiple platforms roughly simultaneously; this meta-correlation exists specifically to surface that broader pattern for SOC teams who might otherwise triage each platform's alerts in isolation.
required_log_sources: All catalogues in this detection library

data_sources.name: cross_catalogue_critical_findings
data_sources.description: Critical-severity findings tagged 'alert-on-all' or 'critical-control' across every catalogue in this library, correlated by time window regardless of source platform.

detection_logic: Three or more distinct source catalogues (identified by detection ID namespace prefix) each producing at least one Critical-severity, alert-on-all-tagged finding within the same rolling 24-hour window.
spl:
index=notable OR (sourcetype="detection:match")
| eval source_catalogue=case(
    match(detection_id, "^AD-"), "active_directory",
    match(detection_id, "^SPL-"), "splunk_esxi_or_platform",
    match(detection_id, "^RH-"), "red_hat",
    match(detection_id, "^F(GT|MG|AZ|AC|CT|EDR|WB|ML|PX|SB|NT)-"), "fortinet",
    match(detection_id, "^IDRAC-"), "dell_idrac",
    match(detection_id, "^ILO-"), "hpe_ilo",
    match(detection_id, "^VCF-"), "vmware_cloud_foundation",
    match(detection_id, "^ARIA-"), "vmware_aria",
    true(), null()
  )
| where isnotnull(source_catalogue) AND severity="critical"
| bucket _time span=24h
| stats dc(source_catalogue) as catalogue_count values(source_catalogue) as catalogues_affected, values(detection_id) as findings by _time
| where catalogue_count >= 3
tuning_guidance: Deploying this detection presumes most or all of the other catalogues in this library are already running in the same Splunk environment; treat it as a capstone/SOC-dashboard-level correlation rather than a typical individual detection, and route matches to the most senior incident-response tier available.
investigation_steps: Review every contributing finding across every affected catalogue.
Assess whether the findings share a common actor, source, or timeframe consistent with a single coordinated campaign versus coincidental unrelated activity.
Stand up a cross-functional incident-response bridge spanning every affected platform team.
response_guidance: Treat as a probable full-environment, multi-platform compromise; engage incident response across every affected platform simultaneously rather than triaging each catalogue's findings independently.
author: Threat Detection Library
performance_guidance: This meta-correlation depends on every catalogue's individual detections being deployed and their matches logged to a common, queryable location (e.g. Splunk ES notable events or a shared detection-match index) — it is an aggregation layer over the rest of the library, not a standalone detection with its own primary telemetry.
attack_mapping_note: This is a meta-correlation layer that depends on every contributing catalogue in this library being deployed and its matches logged to a common, queryable location; it aggregates the rest of the library's detections rather than analyzing its own primary telemetry source.
